  session 98's "the same commit printed two different load counts": an instrument that reads a window
  whose start depends on when you got round to reading it.
- **An unanswered prompt does not stay - it yields the plate.** My own test for "it never asks a third
  time" failed the first time it ran, and correctly: when `fly` runs out of asks, `fire` takes the plate
  (a body was standing in the arena). The test now isolates the mechanism by planting a save that has
  learned the other two. Worth knowing: **the plate is a queue with one slot, not a per-lesson timer.**
- **Sixteen mutations, all caught**, in `.scratch/mutation-check{,2}.mjs` - the copy-the-tree-then-sed-a-
  copy shape, which is now the third time it has been the right instrument (session 101's ablation,
  session 102's ten). The two I expected to be interesting: taking the `isKnown` skip out of `nextLesson`
  (a learned lesson comes back) fails **eight** tests, and deleting the `drawTutorial(ctx)` line from the
  renderer fails the painted-words test, which is the only reason that test exists in that shape.
- **The tick that was owed.** PLAN's *tune every weapon so that none is over 25% better* was left unticked
  although the item under it closed it and session 97 measured the ladder at PASS (1.13x). It was re-run
  on this tree before being ticked - `tools/weapon-ladder.js --seeds 1-16 --shards 10`, nine minutes of
  32 cores: **SWARM 126,460 over LANCE 112,979 = 1.12x against the 1.25x allowed, PASS**, with every gun
  still outlasting the window and `bodies/s` between 6.39 and 7.23. "The tutorial cannot move a run" is a
  claim the fingerprint test and the byte-identical reference trace back up, but a tick that buys its
  verdict wants its own measurement, not an inference.
- **Running the ladder and the suite at the same time is how you find your own flake.** One `perf-probe`
  millisecond test failed while the ladder's ten shards were eating the box and passed on its own -
  exactly what session 98's note predicts ("operations are exact and may be gated tight; milliseconds are
  orders of magnitude and may not"). That test is already on a factor of two for the same reason; under a
  loaded box even a factor of two is a coin toss. Worth knowing before blaming a change for it.

### What should come next
1. **The milestone-10 item that this project cannot do by itself** (line 1587): somebody with a browser
   and an F3 plate has to look at `draw ms` on the owner's laptop. It is the only reading that can
   re-open `bodiesCeil` = 200.
2. **Milestone 11** is now the tail of PLAN: the tutorial (done today), *read every line of text in the
   game and make it short, clear, and consistent*, and `1.0.0`. The text pass should look at
   `tutorial.js`'s three sentences in the same breath as the title's - they are the first words a new
   visitor reads that are not a control list - and at `daily.js`'s four (session 102's note).
3. Still open from earlier sessions: the **shot-speed line** (four seeds cannot tell 0.98 from 1.02;
   `tools/line-ab.js --line bulletSpeed --weapon pulse --seeds 1-16`), the **difficulty band**
   `tools/difficulty-arc.js` still fails, `tools/gun-tune.js` owed from session 96, and session 101's
   unfinished thought that **nothing weighs a painted frame** (a `--paint` door on `tools/alloc-probe.js`).
4. If anyone wants to grow the tutorial, the honest shape is **one more lesson, not a system**: a fourth
   row in `LESSONS`, its latch in `noteLearned`, its moment in `momentIsNow`. Candidates that were
   considered and left out: *the dash into bodies* (a habit, not a control), *the reroll and the banish*
   (the chips on the card table name both), *the vacuum* (it announces itself with a fanfare). Do not
   add a fourth prompt to teach something the arena already teaches.

## Session 104 — A writing pass over every line the game says. Released **0.10.11**

Milestone 10/11's item *read every line of text in the game and make it short, clear, and consistent*.
It turned out to be an instrument problem before it was a writing problem: **half the game's sentences do
not exist until they are painted** (`'RANK ' + held + ' OF ' + max`), so a grep reads parts and not prose.
What shipped is a harvest, a reader, a gate, and the four drifts the reading found. Suite **1851 → 1862**;
the reference run (`--seed 20261006 --trace`) is byte for byte session 101's (10m00s / 73,982 / level 57 /
3,934 kills / 4,934 shards, 7 vacuums, 2036 in), which is what a text-only pass has to look like.

### What landed
- **`tools/headless/text.js`** — `harvestVisit()` boots the game in the stub browser and plays a whole
  visit: title, hangar, codex, settings, mixer readout, a run flying, the level-up table, the pause, the
  wreck's card, the win's card (reached the honest way — park `world.elapsed` at the last fight and put
  the fight down). At each stop it takes back the canvas words the frames asked for and every word the
  page's elements hold, and files them one stop per screen. It also reads **`index.html`** itself, per
  screen, entities decoded, because most interface sentences are markup the code never touches and the
  stub browser has no HTML at all. The visit arrives as a returning player (every ship and perk bought,
  the codex met, four awards won, two runs in the log) on purpose: a filled rack is the rack that prints
  its sentences.
- **`tools/text-survey.js`** — that harvest printed for a human, longest line first, `--counts` for the
  shape of it. 293 lines over ten stops. This is the thing that made the pass possible; read it after any
  large UI change.
- **`test/words.test.mjs`** — the same harvest with the rules on. **The three voices** are what "consistent"
  turned out to mean, and they are written out in that file's header: the interface in caps
  (`HANGAR · BUY SHIPS AND PERKS`), the catalogue in lower case with no full stop (`too heavy to turn, and
  comes apart in two`), a card's copy a sentence that ends like one (`A shot goes through one more body,
  and on to the next.`). Eleven tests: caps everywhere else a player reads (a line is judged *after* the
  catalogue phrases and the clock's `2s`/`15m02s` units are taken out of it), the names all caps, no full
  stop outside a card, the catalogue's 60-character ceiling, the card's 130 (game/upgrades.js's own budget,
  made enforceable; the longest today is 119), the 22 for a card's `what`, a middle dot with room, one bus
  one name, no `1 KILLS`, one wording for the run clock, and a coverage test so the rules cannot quietly
  stop covering anything.
- **The four fixes.** (1) The mixer readout called the effects bus `SOUND` and the settings panel called it
  `SOUNDS` — one machine, two names, now `SOUND` in both with a test that reads the bus names off both
  surfaces. (2) The readout's keys line was the only lower-case sentence on the glass (`M mute    [ ]
  music…`); it is caps like the rows above it, and the stale comment over it that claimed "there is no
  settings page yet" is gone. (3) **`1 KILLS`**: both end cards joined a count to a fixed plural, so the
  win the harvest reached read `1 KILLS · 0 SHARDS · 1 BOSS`; `countWords(count, one, many)` in
  ui/screens.js fixes it and `bossWords` went through it too. (4) The HUD wrote `TIME 902s` while the card
  under it wrote `15m02s` — the same number, two spellings, and `clockWords`'s own comment argued the HUD's
  version was not good enough. It moved to **`core/words.js`** (the palette's argument again: the page and
  the glass may not read each other, so a shared spelling lives in `core/`) and the HUD reads it now. Plus
  two control rows whose comma no other row uses, and the codex's sniper `plants itself, draws a line,
  then fires down it` instead of `bolted down; …`.

### Things that bit, worth remembering
- **`game.screen` answers the whole page**, hidden panels included, so a stop has to say which keys of that
  answer are its own (`READS` in text.js). **A new DOM id is invisible to the harvest unless it is added
  there** — same trap as session 102's note about the harness's own id list, and the coverage test is what
  shouts.
- **Markup lines are kept apart from live page lines.** The file holds templates before a number is put in
  them (`AWARDS 0 OF 0`, a fragment like `· STARDUST`), and a browser collapses runs of spaces in a page
  while the canvas keeps every one — so the middle-dot rule is applied to live lines only, and a template
  fragment is not accused of bad grammar.
- **A wrapped card flavour comes out as fragments** (`Drones circle the ship`, `and grind whatever they`,
  `touch.`), because render/fit.js paints one row per `fillText`. The gate treats a piece of a sentence it
  knows as that sentence; the first version drew the line at eight characters and judged `touch.` as a line
  ending in a full stop. Five is the floor now.
- **Nine mutations, all caught** (`.scratch/word-mutations.mjs`, the copy-sed-run-restore shape). One
  "survived" at first and it was the mutation's fault, not the gate's: the injected flavour was 127
  characters and the ceiling 130. Third time this project has been bitten by a mutation too small to test
  what it claimed to — measure the mutation before believing a survivor.
- The win stop is the only stop where two surfaces show the same fact at once, which is why the clock rule
  is checked there and nowhere else.

### Decisions
- **The developer's plate is a fourth register and stays lower case**, like a terminal: `frame ms`,
  `bodies / ceiling`. The test file says so in its header rather than leaving it as an unexplained hole,
  and the harvest never presses F3.
- **Length ceilings are the writing's, not the layout's.** render/fit.js still guarantees a card cannot
  walk off its frame; the ceilings exist so every card prints at one size and every catalogue line fits a
  column beside a name.
- **`BUILT FROM · NO UPGRADES` was left alone.** A wreck that took no cards reads `WISP · PULSE · BUILT
  FROM · NO UPGRADES`, which is telegraphic, but every better reading either splits one sentence across two
  modules or drops the label the banished lines (`NO TETHER`) are said in the same breath as.
- **`Enter` launches a run and is not mentioned anywhere.** The hint line has no room (session 102) and an
  undiscovered convenience is not a lie; `test/controls.test.mjs` knows it works.

### What should come next
1. **Milestone 11 is one item from the end: release `1.0.0`.** The only other open item in PLAN is the
   browser half of the performance pass, which needs a real GPU and an F3 plate.
2. **If the survey is ever widened, do it as a second persona, not a second assertion.** The first-run
   prompts (game/tutorial.js) need a visit that has never flown and the empty racks need a save that has
   bought nothing; one game lives in a process, so it wants `--persona fresh|veteran` and a child process
   each. The ungated surfaces today are the toast (render/toast.js — its own tests read its words) and the
   F3 plate (by choice).
3. **Any new line of text has to say which voice it speaks.** Caps for the interface, lower case for a
   description of a thing, a full sentence on a card. If it is none of those, that is the moment to notice.
4. Still open from session 103: the **shot-speed line** (`tools/line-ab.js --line bulletSpeed --weapon
   pulse --seeds 1-16`), the **difficulty band** `tools/difficulty-arc.js` still fails, `tools/gun-tune.js`
   owed from session 96, and session 101's **`--paint` door** on `tools/alloc-probe.js`.

## Session 105 — A thumb: the stick appears where it lands, one button dashes, the gun runs itself. Released **0.10.12**

Milestone 9's *Touch support*. PLAN section 6's sentence is three halves and they belong to three layers:
`input/touch.js` knows where a thumb has to land to mean something, the stick lean is written into the
same descriptor WASD writes into, and the aiming and the trigger are `game/assists.js` - the two switches
that were already written. Suite **1862 → 1884** (13 driving tests in `test/touch.test.mjs`, 9 picture
tests in `test/touch-art.test.mjs`); the reference run (`--seed 20261006 --trace`) is byte for byte
session 101's again (10m00s / 73,982 / level 57 / 3,934 kills / 4,934 shards, 7 vacuums, 2036 in), which
is the whole point of the "a mouse visit is the visit it always was" half of the test file.

### What landed
- **`src/input/touch.js`** (new). A floating stick: a touch that begins left of half the glass while a run
  is being flown becomes the stick, wherever the thumb landed, with its reach a share of the shorter window
  side (0.19, clamped 46-90 px) and a dead zone of 18% of that reach, so a resting thumb is not a lean. The
  push is a vector of at most 1, so half the stick is half the ship and the end of it is the ship's own top
  speed (`steer` clamps the target speed). A dash button bottom-right (radius 0.15 of the short side, clamped
  44-76, inset 26 and lifted 46 px clear of the XP bar), one press = one `touchTaps.dash`. Every touch is
  `preventDefault`ed (a browser allowed to scroll eats the gesture a stick is made of, and the synthesised
  click after a tap would answer a card twice). `clearThumb()` runs on blur.
- **`flying()` is the one question the input layer asks the game**, answered in `main.js`'s `initInput`.
  While a run is being flown, the glass is a control surface; while it is not, a touch is exactly the press
  a click already was - `noteGlass(x, y)` in `input/mouse.js` leaves the point where the cursor keeps its
  own, then `onPress` runs, so the title launches, a card is answered and the wreck restarts without a
  single screen learning the word "finger".
- **`src/render/touch.js`** (new). Ring, knob, button and the word `DASH`, painted from `dashButton()` and
  `stickReach()` - the input layer's own numbers - so the ring an eye sees and a thumb presses are one ring
  by construction. Only while a run is flying and not paused, and only for a thumb visit.
- **`game/assists.js` now has a default per hand.** Two maps instead of one: `moved` (has a hand ever said
  a value for this row) and `switches` (what it said), plus `thumbVisit`. `on(id)` answers a moved row from
  what it was moved to and an unmoved one from its row's `default` - or from `true` under a thumb. The save
  writes only rows a hand moved (`written()`, used by `stepRow`) so a default cannot be frozen into the save
  by a sibling row being moved; `standing()` is the unchanged "every row's place" that `stats()` reads. A
  lock left behind by a switch that has just been turned off is dropped in `driveAssists`.
- **`main.js`**: a tap is allowed back into a held run when the visit flies on a thumb (a click is still
  refused - the left button is the gun), asked *before* the panel rule because the pause is a panel and the
  settings rack over a held run still owns the screen. `stats().thumbUsed` for the tools.
- **`ui/screens.js`**: `showPause(run, onGlass)` writes the rack's own line - `TAP TO GO BACK TO THE RUN`
  or the `ESC OR P` one. New `#pauseHint` id, in `index.html` and in the harness's `ELEMENT_IDS`.
- **`render/cards.js`**: the line under the cards is `1 2 3 OR TAP` for a thumb run.
- **Harness**: `touchDown/touchMove/touchUp(x, y, id)` build real touch events with `changedTouches` and a
  `preventDefault` that counts (`game.touchPrevented`), and `screen.pauseHint`.

### Decisions that will be asked about again
- **A thumb is the two assists, on - as a default, not as a force.** The first cut forced them inside
  `driveAssists`, which meant a thumb run could not take the trigger back: a row it moved itself would be
  overruled every frame. Now the thumb changes what an unmoved row ships at, and a row a hand moved wins in
  whichever direction it was moved. That keeps PLAN's sentence ("auto-aim and auto-fire are on for touch
  runs") and the two rows' reason to exist (accessibility, and they are the same two rows) both true.
- **The thumb's flag belongs to the visit, not to the finger.** `thumb.used` is set when a control *claims*
  a touch and never unset; lifting the thumb does not hand the trigger back, so a run keeps shooting while
  the thumb is off the glass. `test/touch.test.mjs` states this on purpose with a second window after the
  lift - a phone has no trigger to hold, and a run that stopped firing every time a thumb rested would read
  as broken.
- **A tap is not a control claim**, so a touchscreen laptop that caught one accidental brush is not a visit
  that asked for auto-aim. This is why `used` is not set by `noteGlass`.
- **The racks stay keyboard racks** (hangar, codex, settings). Section 6 asks that all screens work with
  keyboard alone and with a gamepad; a touch on a rack row today is an unclaimed touch, which is nothing at
  all - deliberate, and recorded here so it does not look like an oversight. Same for the static launch
  lines in `index.html`, which still say `CLICK`; nothing in JS writes them (see below).

### Things that bit, worth remembering
- **`enemyAt` from `tools/headless/scripted.js` puts the body in the crowd; `makeEnemy` does not.** A test
  that plants a body with `makeEnemy` aims at nothing and shoots nothing.
- **An enemy's hull ceiling is `maxhp`, lower case** (`kinds.js` sets `enemy.maxhp = enemy.hp`). A test that
  reads `body.maxHp` fails with `NaN worth`, which took a lap to read.
- **Emptying `world.enemies` by hand leaves `world.aimLock` pointing at a body that has gone**, and
  `takeAim` will keep holding it (`targetable` asks only `hp > 0 && immune <= 0`). Plant one body and watch
  it twice instead of clearing the crowd between two halves of a test.
- **`stats().bullets > 0` is a flaky proof of auto-fire** - shots land and die, and a single planted body
  can drink a whole volley. The honest proof is hull lost on a body with enough hull to survive the window.
- **A mashed dash is never "ready"** (session 9's trap again): the mash fires the instant the wait is paid,
  so no frame ever has `dashCd === 0 && dashLeft === 0`. Count dash *starts* over a bounded window instead,
  and bound the loop by construction rather than by waiting for a condition.
- **`game.words()` keeps every space the painter wrote.** `haloText` lines are separated with three spaces
  and one `·`; `words()[i]` is not whitespace-collapsed, so match a whole line exactly or use
  `game.texts()` and `startsWith`/`endsWith`. `texts()` returns `{text,x,y,w,size,align,stroke}` and a
  haloed word appears twice, once stroked and once filled.
- **One boot per process means every test has to ask for its own run** (`await fly()`, `await running()`).
  A run left sitting in a crowd dies eventually and then the next test fails for a reason that has nothing
  to do with it; a filtered run (`--test-name-pattern`) also skips whatever launched it. Each test lifts
  every thumb it puts down: one live thumb hides the next, because the stick belongs to the first finger
  that claimed it.
- `touchmove` is a per-event `changedTouches` list, so the harness hands over one finger per event; and the
  browser's own touch→click synthesis is dead only because every handler calls `preventDefault`, which is
  what `game.touchPrevented` exists to keep true.

### What should come next
1. **Milestone 9's three remaining items: key rebinding, gamepad support, colour-blind palette.** Each is
   smaller than this one. Gamepad wants the same treatment the thumb got - a descriptor field, and painted
   geometry read from the input layer's numbers.
2. **If anyone wants the launch lines to speak to a thumb**: `#titleScreen`'s and `#overScreen`'s `.hint`
   lines are static in `index.html` and no JS writes them, so it wants a `showStart`-shaped hook (the title
   is what `hideScreens` leaves visible, not a screen anything raises). A tap already works on both.
   Worth doing in the same breath as racks-by-touch, if that is ever wanted.
3. Rack touch, if it is ever wanted, also wants the `preventDefault` on `touchstart` revisited for touches
   that begin over the DOM panels - a panel is not a control surface, and today the glass is told not to
   scroll everywhere.
4. Still open from session 103: the **shot-speed line** (`tools/line-ab.js --line bulletSpeed --weapon
   pulse --seeds 1-16`), the **difficulty band** `tools/difficulty-arc.js` still fails, `tools/gun-tune.js`
   owed from session 96, and session 101's **`--paint` door** on `tools/alloc-probe.js`. Then milestone 10's
   last item: the browser half of the performance pass, and `1.0.0`.

## Session 106 — A pad: two sticks and a shoulder. Released **0.10.13**

Milestone 9's *Gamepad support*. Done out of PLAN's order (key rebinding was the item above it) for a
reason worth keeping: the two remaining M9 items are a key-table and a palette, and this was the second
of the three **device** items, which wants the same shape the thumb got - a descriptor field, one honest
answer to "which hand is speaking", and a test that a visit that never met the device is unchanged.
Suite **1884 → 1899** (14 in `test/gamepad.test.mjs`, 1 in `test/debug.test.mjs`); the reference run
(`--seed 20261006 --trace`) is byte for byte session 105's again (10m00s / 73,982 / level 57 / 3,934
kills / 4,934 shards, 7 vacuums, 2036 in) with the whole feature in the tree.

### What landed
- **`src/input/gamepad.js`** (new). Polled once a frame from `readInput()`, not listened for:
  `gamepadconnected` says a device arrived and no event says a button moved, so a poll finds a pad the
  frame it is plugged in and stops flying the ship the frame it is taken away, with no listener and no
  unsubscribe. `navigator.getGamepads()` is guarded for absence (it is absent in Node, and in a browser
  without the API) and for a sparse list. Two dead zones (`MOVE_DEAD 0.2`, `AIM_DEAD 0.32` - the aim's
  is also the trigger's, so it gets the roomier one) and a push **remeasured from the zone**, so just
  clearing the line is a crawl and not a jump to a third of top speed (a test measures it: <20% of
  maxSpeed at 0.26 of a stick's travel, then 4x that at full).
- **Two families of pad, told apart by axis count** (`FOUR_AXIS` / `SIX_AXIS`): under five axes the
  right trigger is button 7 and Start is 9; five or more and the trigger is axis 5 and Start is 7.
  Everything they agree on (axes 0-3, A at 0, RB at 5) is read unconditionally, so a pad that fits
  neither still flies; the worst a mis-guessed Start does is hold the run on a stick click. Buttons are
  read as object, number or boolean because browsers have used all three.
- **The right stick is the trigger** (PLAN's wording, kept literal): `pad.firing` is "the stick is
  leaned", a hold and not a press. `input.firing = mouse.down || pad.firing`.
- **A stick is a direction, not a place on the glass**, which is the one thing that stopped the pad
  being "just another pointer". The descriptor gained `stickAim` + `aimDirX/aimDirY`; `main.js` either
  calls `resolveAim` (pointer → arena, through the camera) or `pointFromStick` (arena point
  `STICK_AIM_REACH = 500` px in front of the ship). From `world.player.x/y` and **not** the interpolated
  position: the step reads the aim too, and an interpolating ship would shiver the angle every gun is
  fired along; the camera lean is the only other reader and it smooths the ~3 px difference away. The
  reach is a rendering number - `player.js` takes an arctangent of the gap, so any reach aims the same.
- **Which hand owns the nose** is one variable in `input/index.js` (`aimHand`, plus a remembered
  `pointerCount`): the stick owns it while leaned and keeps it when it comes home (the nose stays where
  that hand left it); a changed `mouse.moves` takes it back. `input/mouse.js` grew that counter, bumped
  by `mousemove` **and** by `noteGlass`, so a thumb's tap counts as the pointer having spoken. First
  cut was two counters compared (`aimPushes > moves`), which was not "last" at all - one deliberate
  mouse move lost to five stick pushes and the pointer could not take the aim back.
- **A is the launch key and Start is the pause**, answered from the poll straight into the same handlers
  a keydown answers (`onConfirm`, `onPause`), not queued: a frame that ran no step is still a frame in
  which a press expects an answer. Nothing else on a pad is bound - see the decisions below.
- `pad.name` is the id cut at the first `(` (a browser's id is "Wireless Controller (STANDARD GAMEPAD
  Vendor: 0x045d...)") and is `''` whenever no pad is being read, so an unplugged pad cannot be reported
  as a plugged one. It is in `STARFALL.stats().pad` and in the F3 panel's new **HANDS** row
  (`gamepad  none` / the name, and `thumb  on/off`) - the only place the game admits to watching for a
  pad. `index.html`'s controls list gained a GAMEPAD row.
- **Harness**: `setPad(state|null)`, `padAxis(i, v)`, `padButton(i, down)`. Node's `globalThis.navigator`
  is a **getter** and cannot be assigned (TypeError in strict mode), so the stub uses
  `Object.defineProperty`. `{}` is a four-axis pad at rest; `{ axes: [0,0,0,0,0,-1] }` is a six-axis one
  with its triggers parked at -1. `padAxis`/`padButton` throw with no pad in, so a test that leans a
  stick that is not there fails instead of silently measuring nothing.

### Decisions that will be asked about again
- **Only the three controls PLAN asks for, plus A and Start.** The cards, hangar, codex and settings stay
  keyboard/mouse racks: a pad in a browser is never the only device (it arrives beside a keyboard and is
  polled beside it), and a fake cursor on the glass is a whole second interface - which card is lit, what
  moves it, what clicks it, what happens over nothing - bigger than the one plan line it would serve. Same
  reasoning the thumb's note records for the same racks.
- **The pad does not switch the assists on.** The thumb had to (a finger has no cursor and no trigger); a
  pad's right stick *is* the cursor and *is* the trigger. If a save has AUTO-AIM on it wins, exactly as it
  wins over a mouse - that is what the switch is for.
- **`aimHand` is not reset by `clearInput()`/blur.** Losing focus does not change who spoke last; the pad
  lets go of its sticks by being polled anyway. Consequence to know: a second run on the same page starts
  with whichever hand last pointed the nose (the pointer behaves the same way, keeping its own last place).
- The move ordering is keys → pad → thumb, thumb last ("a finger on the glass is the most recent thing a
  hand did"), stated in a comment and pinned by a test that leans all three at once.

### Things that bit, worth remembering
- **`Pool.stats().spawned` is a lifetime count, not a per-run one** - `resetRun` clears a pool but does not
  wind the counter back. A snapshot that puts `bullets.stats().spawned` in it and compares two runs will
  differ by the shots the first run fired. Take the delta from the start of the run.
- **A thumb is never picked back up** (session 105's decision), so any test that puts one down leaves
  AUTO-FIRE and AUTO-AIM switched on for the rest of the process - `driveAssists` sets `thumbVisit` and
  nothing clears it. It made a "the guns stop when the stick comes home" assertion fail 2 shots out of 38,
  and it would have made the aim tests lie. **The thumb test is last in `test/gamepad.test.mjs` on purpose**
  and says so in a comment; anything that measures a hand holding its own gun must come before it.
- A test that checks the pointer takes the aim back must remember `moveMouse` is one bump of the counter.
- Auto-fire makes "is it firing" unmeasurable by counting shots; with the assists off (the ordinary case)
  `world.bullets.stats().spawned` is the honest instrument.

### What should come next
1. Milestone 9 is down to **key rebinding** and the **colour-blind palette**, then its release item.
   Rebinding is the bigger of the two and wants a decision first about scope: the game has ~20 keys, but
   four movement keys + dash + the panel letters are the set a non-QWERTY hand actually needs, and the
   settings rack is arrow-driven, so a rebind row needs a "listening" state that Esc does not cancel
   (Esc is the pause and does not close panels here). The palette is a `settings.js` row with choices plus
   the "brightness and shape as well as hue" half, which is an art decision about enemy kinds and shards.
2. If a pad ever gets the racks, the honest shape is a *selection* per panel (D-pad moves a cursor, A
   takes it) rather than a glass cursor - the settings and the hangar already have a row cursor; the cards
   do not, and `render/cards.js` already paints one card `hovered`, so a card cursor is cheaper than it
   looks.
3. Still open from session 103: the **shot-speed line** (`tools/line-ab.js --line bulletSpeed --weapon
   pulse --seeds 1-16`), the **difficulty band** `tools/difficulty-arc.js` still fails, `tools/gun-tune.js`
   owed from session 96, and session 101's **`--paint` door** on `tools/alloc-probe.js`. Then milestone 10's
   last item: the browser half of the performance pass, and `1.0.0`.

## Session 107 — The keys are yours to move: a CONTROLS rack inside the settings. Released **0.10.14**

Milestone 9's *Key rebinding*. Suite **1899 → 1928** (15 in `test/keymap.test.mjs`, 14 in
`test/keys.test.mjs`); the reference run (`--seed 20261006 --trace`) is byte for byte session 106's again
(10m00s / 73,982 / level 57 / 3,934 kills / 4,934 shards, 7 vacuums, 2036 in) with the whole feature in
the tree - which is the check that mattered most here: a key table is not allowed to nudge a single die.

### What landed
- **`src/core/keymap.js`** (new) is the one table: `ACTIONS` (id, name, what it is, the shipped code, and
  what the page writes for it), `KEY_CODES` (what may be taken, and why each one may), and four lookups -
  `codeFor`, `actionFor`, `wordsOf`, `tableAsWords`. `rebind()` **swaps instead of stealing**: giving DASH
  the key that HANGAR wore leaves hangar answering the key dash just left, so the table is always a
  one-to-one map and a player can never end up with a control nothing answers. `restore(id)` puts one row
  back, `changedCount()` says whether anything moved, `loadFromSave()`/`saveKeys()` keep it. A shipped key
  writes nothing to the document - a save that has to remember the defaults is a save that has to be right
  about them forever.
- **Thirteen bindable controls**: up/down/left/right, dash, pause, give up, hangar, codex, settings, daily,
  reroll, mute. **Fixed forever**: `Space`/`Enter` (the launch, and the aim-during-a-run), the numbers (they
  name a card or a ship on every build), `[ ] - =` (the sliders are two rows on the settings panel, which is
  the same number of arrow presses away on any keyboard), `F3`, the arrows, and **`Escape`**. The `Esc`
  decision is the one worth keeping: a key that cancels a rebinding cannot be the key a rebinding takes,
  so the PAUSE row prints `P` and the pause line says `ESC OR P` - two keys, one meaning, still.
- **The four arrows are always movement as well** (`input/index.js`: `held('left') || keys.ArrowLeft`).
  They are the pair a keyboard with no letters to spare still has, and no panel can be put up over a run
  being flown, so a rack's cursor and the ship never want them on the same frame. This is what makes an
  arrow-driven panel and arrow-driven flight coexist without a key ever meaning two things at once.
- **`input/keyboard.js` hard-codes nothing that a panel can offer a row for.** One `actionFor(code)`
  lookup, one `runAction` switch. It also grew `captureKeys(fn)`: one listener in front of everything for
  exactly one keypress (no held state written, no handler told, `preventDefault` on everything it swallows).
  The four arrows are **never** sent to the capture - they are the panel's own verbs and the table will not
  accept one as a binding, so swallowing them would leave a player stuck in a waiting row.
- **A CONTROLS rack behind one door on the settings panel** (`index.html` `#keysScreen`, wearing the
  settings panel's CSS because a row there *is* a settings row whose value happens to be a key). `→` asks
  the keyboard, `←` puts the shipped key back, the hint line changes while a row waits, and the waiting row
  is amber **while keeping its cyan cursor** - the amber is the cursor lit differently, not a second light.
  `main.js` owns the panel's furniture (`keysCursor`, `waitingRow`, `openKeysPanel`, `backToSettings`,
  `moveKeysRow`, `changeKeysRow`, `takeCapturedKey`) and `ownsTheScreen()` is now `settingsIsUp() ||
  keysIsUp()`, so the launch key and the number keys stand aside for both.
- **Refused presses stay silent**: a modifier, a function key, a number or an arrow given to a waiting row
  changes nothing and the row keeps waiting - the same bargain every refused press in this game strikes.
  `Escape` is the way out of a row, and the only thing it does there (the pause keeps its meaning the moment
  the rack stops asking; `takeCapturedKey` is the safety net for a rack taken down under a rebinding).
- **Nothing is left holding an old key.** `ui/screens.js` `KEY_LABELS` lists every span `index.html`
  carries for a movable key (18 of them: the title's list, both racks' hints, the pause's two lines, both
  cards, the rack's own way-back line) and `paintKeyWords()` writes all of them from the table at boot and
  after every move. `game/tutorial.js`'s lessons now name their *controls* (`keys: ['up','left',...]`) and
  `saysOf()` spells the line out of the live table, so a hand that rebound its keys before its first run is
  taught its own keys. `showPause` composes its own line the same way.
- **Save**: a `keys` section with `binds` (control → code), a new `KINDS.mapping` validator beside
  `counts`, and the same entry-by-entry bargains - one bad code drops that row and keeps its neighbours.
- **Harness**: `game.text(id)` (a generic readout, so a test does not need a field per label), the
  `keysRows` snapshot with `chosen` and `waiting`, and `keysHidden`/`keysNote`/`keysHint`. `tools/headless/text.js`
  now walks through the door so the new rack is in the words survey and `test/words.test.mjs`.

### Things that bit, worth remembering
- **`KINDS.mapping` landed between `counts`' doc comment and `counts` itself** and left the table with an
  orphaned doc block. When adding a validator, put it *before* the previous one's comment, then re-read the
  whole object once.
- **A panel that steals the keyboard has to give it back on every path**, not just its own. `Escape`, `←`,
  `→` and moving the cursor all drop the ask, and `takeCapturedKey` starts with
  `if (!keysIsUp()) { stopListening(); return; }` for the paths that take the rack down from somewhere else
  (a blur, a pause, a hangar). Without the guard a swallowed keypress is lost and the player presses twice.
- **`test/keys.test.mjs`'s `goTo` walks with `while`, and a rack that is not up answers no rows** - the
  first draft hung the suite on a `while (chosenRow() < index)` over an empty rack. `goTo` asserts the rack
  is up before it walks anything. (`node --test` with no timeout will sit on that forever; `timeout 200` is
  worth it while a new driver test is being written.)
- **Rebinding the settings key changes how the tests get anywhere.** `openRack()`/`closePanels()` in
  `test/keys.test.mjs` read `codeFor('settings')` instead of pressing `KeyO`, and every test that leaves a
  moved key must put it back (`shippedAgain()`), or a later test in the same process cannot find the door.
- **Three markup tests read `index.html` as text** and broke the moment a key became a live span
  (`test/daily.test.mjs`'s title hint, `test/victory-card.test.mjs`'s win hint, which captured `[^<]*`).
  The win-hint one now strips tags before matching. Expect this again: any line that gets a live key is a
  line a file-reading test has to be told about.
- The settings panel grew a row, so four tests that print its row list by name had to grow too
  (`settings`, `assists`, two in `volume`), including the cursor arithmetic in `volume` (`MUSIC` is row 5
  now, `MUTE` row 7). A row inserted in the middle of a rack is not a middle-only change.

### What should come next
1. Milestone 9 has one item left: the **colour-blind palette** - a `settings.js` row with choices, plus the
   harder half, which is "brightness and shape as well as hue" across the enemy kinds and the shards. That
   is an art decision about ~20 bodies before it is a code change; `tools/palette-check.js` and session 101's
   notes on contrast are the place to start, and `--paint` on `tools/alloc-probe.js` is still owed from 101.
2. Milestone 9's last item is its release checklist, then milestone 10's browser half of the performance
   pass and `1.0.0`. Still open from earlier: the **shot-speed line** (`tools/line-ab.js --line bulletSpeed
   --weapon pulse --seeds 1-16`), the **difficulty band** `tools/difficulty-arc.js` still fails, and
   `tools/gun-tune.js` owed from session 96.
3. Small things this session noticed and did not do: the rack's rows are all one line each and a very narrow
   window leans on `fitKeys()` (it fits, but it is the tightest panel in the game now); and a pad has no way
   into the racks (session 106's note 2 still stands - a selection per panel, not a glass cursor).

## Session 108 — The menu announces itself: the device is built at boot, any press wakes it. Released **0.10.15**

The owner's hotfix: *"The menu music does not start unless I hit H to enter the hangar. The menu music
should announce itself on the root menu."* They were right and the bug was ours. Suite **1928 → 1936**;
the reference run (`--seed 20261006 --trace`) is byte for byte session 107's again (10m00s / 73,982 /
level 57 / 3,934 kills / 4,934 shards, 7 vacuums, 2036 in), and `--audio` still prints its pattern line.

### What landed
- **`openAudioDevice()` (audio/engine.js) is called at boot**, in `main.js` right after `restoreAudio()`.
  That was the missing half: the device had only ever been built by a press, and the press that builds it
  is usually the one that launches a run, so a browser that *would* have let the title screen make a
  sound on its own - no autoplay rule, or one that remembers this origin playing audio before - was never
  once asked. Now the ask happens before the first frame and, where the browser says yes, the song is
  playing before a hand has done anything. Two new test files hold the two kinds of browser:
  `test/menu-track-boot.test.mjs` (`autoplay: true` - the song is up with no press at all, the title pad
  stands down under it, a run still takes the bus back) and `test/menu-track-wake.test.mjs` (the ordinary
  strict browser - device built and asleep, nothing spent, and the first press waking it).
- **`audioIsHeard()` is the new question, and it replaced `getContext() !== null` in both places that
  write ahead of the frame** - `updateMenuTrack` (audio/track.js) and `updateMusic` (audio/music.js). A
  device that exists but is asleep has a clock that is not advancing, so a note scheduled at
  `currentTime` is not a note that is heard, it is a note that waits; thirty steps of the past written
  into a stopped clock is the tune thrown at the wall on the wake. The sequencer now leaves `nextAt`
  where it is and re-anchors on the first frame that finds the clock running, which is the same rule it
  already applied to a clock that jumped forward.
- **`wakeAudio()` is the engine's one door to `resume()`** (promise caught, callback-only browsers
  forgiven). It is called from presses and from nowhere else: `initAudio()` (every action handler that
  already called it), main.js's new first-press listeners, `play()` in track.js, and `auditionMusic`.
  The frame loop does not ask any more - `updateMusic` used to `resume()` on every frame while the device
  slept, and a browser only ever answers that question the first time.
- **`AUDIO_WAKE_EVENTS` (main.js): `keydown`, `mousedown`, `pointerdown`, `touchstart`**, permanent
  window listeners on `wakeAudio`. A press the game does not answer is still a press, and still the
  browser's answer to "may this page make a sound" - which is the exact hole the owner fell into (they
  pressed `H`, which answers, and got the song). They stay on: waking a running device is nothing, and a
  browser can fall asleep on its own.
- **A visit that came back muted gets a device too.** The mute is a knob on the bus above both buses, not
  an absence of a device, so pressing `M` on the title is now the moment the menu starts singing instead
  of a trip to a panel. The bytes are still not spent on a muted visit - that door is in track.js, where
  it was.
- **Two reasons the title is quiet are now said out loud** in `menuTrackLedger().reason` - "asleep: no
  browser lets a page make a sound before a press" and "this visit came back muted" - so `STARFALL.stats().menuTrack`
  answers the visitor who wonders. `waiting` was the whole answer before and it answered nothing.
- **The stub browser models the autoplay rule at last** (tools/headless/harness.js): the fake device is
  built `suspended`, `resume()` is honoured only once the harness has fired a real gesture (`GESTURES` in
  `fire()` - a mouse *moving` is not one), `bootGame({ autoplay: true })` is a browser that lets the page
  play, and `game.audioState` says `none | suspended | running`. `game.audio.resumes` counts the asks,
  which is how a test can prove the frame loop never tried to buy what only a press buys.
- Docs: track.js's header, engine.js's three new doc blocks, `updateMusic`'s, README's music paragraph,
  and the request itself is archived with the note on what shipped.

### Decisions worth keeping
- **The device is asked for at boot even though it may be refused.** The refusal costs a device that
  plays nothing and, in Chrome, one console line ("The AudioContext was not allowed to start") - which is
  the browser describing the very thing the owner asked for. `openAudioDevice()` deliberately does *not*
  call `resume()`: a browser that allows it hands out a running device anyway, and a resume asked by a
  frame cannot land, so asking would only add noise.
- **Sound effects are not gated on audibility, on purpose.** Every sfx is caused by a press and that same
  press wakes the clock, so gating them would swallow the launch tick - the one sound a first visit must
  never lose. The only things that write *ahead* of a frame (the sequencer's half second of lookahead,
  the recording) are the ones that have to wait for a running clock.
- **A blocked browser whose first press is the launch still never hears the menu**, and nothing in this
  session pretends otherwise: there is no way to be heard before a press, and the launch press has already
  left the menu by the time it is granted. The honest shapes of "hear the song again after a run" would
  be a way back to the title (the death's card has two keys and could hold a third), not a second song.
- The wake listeners are permanent rather than one-shot. Two `if`s per press is cheaper than the state
  machine that retires them, and one of them has to survive in case the browser suspends the context on
  its own and needs waking again.

### Things that bit, worth remembering
- **`game.audio.voices` counts the master graph's three gain nodes**, so "the title screen plays nothing"
  is no longer a `=== 0` assertion. `test/audio.test.mjs` and `test/ui-sound.test.mjs` now snapshot the
  graph's count and assert it does not *move*, which says what they meant anyway.
- **A test that calls `initAudio()` to stand in for "the browser's first click" no longer gets a running
  clock** - the stub is right to refuse it, because nothing pressed anything. `test/music.test.mjs` boots
  `autoplay: true` and dropped its `initAudio()`. `mix` and `noise` were unaffected and stayed as they
  were: sfx are not gated, so their buses work fine on a sleeping device.
- One game per process, so "the browser that lets us" and "the browser that does not" are two test files
  and not two tests. `test/menu-track.test.mjs` (the muted visit) keeps its own file for the same reason.
- `state: 'interrupted'` (iOS's word for a stopped clock) counts as not heard, next to `suspended`. A
  context with no `state` at all - an old browser - counts as heard, so it keeps the behaviour it had.
- The release script refuses a dirty tree, and **`git status --porcelain` counts untracked files**:
  `tools/colour-lab.js` had been sitting untracked since session 107 (an Oklab measurement module whose
  two named consumers - `tools/palette-check.js`, `test/palette-read.test.mjs` - were never written). It
  is now `.scratch/colour-lab.js`, which `.gitignore` already covers, so the palette session starts from
  it instead of writing it again. Nothing tracked was touched.

### What should come next
1. Milestone 9 has the **colour-blind palette** left: a `settings.js` row with choices plus "brightness
   and shape as well as hue" across the ~20 enemy bodies and the shards - an art decision before it is a
   code change, and `.scratch/colour-lab.js` is the measurement half of it (pull it back into `tools/`
   with the `palette-check.js` it was written for). Then milestone 9's release checklist.
2. Still owed from earlier sessions: the **shot-speed line** (`tools/line-ab.js --line bulletSpeed
   --weapon pulse --seeds 1-16`), the **difficulty band** `tools/difficulty-arc.js` still fails,
   `tools/gun-tune.js` from session 96, and session 101's **`--paint` door** on `tools/alloc-probe.js`.
   Then milestone 10's browser half of the performance pass, and `1.0.0`.
3. Noticed and not done: the title's own generated pad is now audible on a permissive browser before the
   recording arrives, which is the fade the design wanted - but if the recording is *missing* on such a
   visit (a release without `assets/`), the title now plays the pad where it used to be silent until the
   first press. That is the right sound, and it is worth one line in the palette-of-sounds sense: the pad
   is 0.02 per voice and it is what the sequencer has always played there.

## Session 109 — The palette was measured: Oklab, five eyes, and the shipped colours held

Suite **1936 → 1957** (10 in `test/colour-lab.test.mjs`, 11 in `test/palette-read.test.mjs`). The
reference run (`--seed 20261006 --trace`) is byte for byte session 108's again (10m00s / 73,982 /
level 57 / 3,934 kills / 4,934 shards, 7 vacuums, 2036 in) - and it had better be, because **nothing
in `src/` changed at all**. That is the outcome of this session, not a near-miss: the milestone item
is "colour-blind palette", four sessions said "measure it first", and the measurement said the game
as shipped is already sound. Nothing released: the player can see nothing here (yet).

### What landed
- **`tools/colour-lab.js`** - pulled back out of `.scratch/` (where session 108 parked it) into the
  `tools/` it was written for. Oklab: linear-light channels → three cone-like responses → cube root
  → `{L, a, b}`, plus `oklch`, CIE `L*`, `over()` (compositing a translucent colour onto the sky it
  is drawn on), and the colour-vision half: `VISIONS` (five eyes, each named by the axes it *keeps*),
  `separation()` (the largest axis gap, in steps), and `worstVision()`. **It had a real bug**:
  tritanopia was wired to keep `['L','b']`, the same pair as the two red-green eyes, when the whole
  point of a blue-blind eye is that it keeps `a` and loses `b` - the file's own prose said so two
  lines above. Fixed, and `test/colour-lab.test.mjs` now asserts each eye's `keeps` against its name
  and shows a hand-built colour going *to zero* along the axis that eye has lost.
- **`tools/sights.js`** - the question, which is the half that actually matters. A palette cannot be
  audited as a list of colours; "is `#ff4d6d` far enough from `#ff2d55`" has no answer until you say
  what each is *for*, how big a thing it is painted on, and what shape the eye gets. So: 19 sights
  (nine bodies read out of `BALANCE.kinds`, an enemy shot, the sniper's beam, a bomber's blast, the
  ship's mine, the ship, its shot, a shard small and large, the wall, a boss's cage), each with a
  **meaning** (`harm` / `help` / `self` / `place`), a **form** (the silhouette the renderer really
  draws, not the balance table's `sides`), and a **size**. Plus `promiseOf(a, b)`, the promise
  matrix, and `auditSights()` / `auditSky()` - which the report and the tests both call, so they
  cannot disagree.
- **`tools/palette-check.js`** - the report: what the eye is handed, every *promised* pair against
  its bar, every pair with nothing at stake under its own heading, every sight against the sky it sits
  on. `--all` for the whole matrix, `--only shard` for one corner of it, `--strict` to exit non-zero.
- **Twenty-one tests.** The ruler's (`the extremes of brightness are the extremes`, `each eye is
  blind along exactly the axis its name says`, `a translucent colour is measured where it lands, not
  as written`, `an eye nobody measured is an error, not a free pass`) and the palette's
  (`nothing that can hurt you is the colour of nothing that can help you`, `a shard is never mistaken
  for a threat`, `their shot is not your shot`, `every sight can be seen at all`,
  `what is promised, and what is not`). Three of them are guards on the audit itself:
  **`every enemy the game can spawn is in the table`** (asks `BALANCE.kinds` who is in the crowd, so a
  new kind cannot be quietly unmeasured), **`the sizes the table measures are the sizes the renderer
  draws`** (reads `SHARD_BODY`/`BIG_SHARD_BODY`/`MINE_BODY`/`MINE_SPIKE` out of `render/entities.js`,
  because `tools/` may not import it), and **`the promise can fail - it is a guard and not a
  formality`** (paints a shard in an enemy shot's colour and asserts the audit shouts).

### The promise, as it ended up - and why each cut is where it is
PLAN section 6's line is "a colour-blind palette that separates harmful and helpful by brightness and
shape as well as hue". Turned into something that can fail, in `tools/sights.js`:

- **A pair with no harm in it is reported, not promised.** The confusion that costs a run is
  harm-vs-help, harm-vs-self (their shot is not your shot) and harm-vs-boundary (an edge that looks
  like a hazard, or a hazard that looks like an edge). Two harms that share a colour cost a wrong
  gun choice; a help and a self cost a walk over nothing. That is the whole reason the audit reports
  84 of its 171 pairs instead of demanding nine bodies be a step apart from each other in nine
  unrelated colours.
- **Where shape cannot tell a pair apart, colour must** - a full step on every axis an eye keeps.
  "Alike" means the same form, or sizes within 1.3× of each other. Where the forms differ (a band of
  light and a five-pixel diamond) colour has to do most of it (0.55) and *nothing* is promised about
  brightness: PLAN's phrase read the other way round - brightness is what has to be there when the
  shape is not enough.
- **A boundary is promised hue and not brightness.** The wall and a boss's cage are drawn where no
  body can be, and they are cool because they are the world stopping; a wall is where the wall is.
- **The strict bar is a red-green eye's.** ~1 man in 12 is red-green colour blind and keeps the
  blue-yellow axis and brightness - that is what `RED_GREEN_EYES` measures. The no-hue eye (achromatopsia,
  about 1 in 30,000) is promised a whole step of brightness only where a pair is *alike in shape*, and
  nothing otherwise: a mint diamond and a cyan bolt of the same brightness are two objects to anyone
  who can see that a diamond is not a bolt. Bent further, this rule would repaint the arena for one
  visitor in thirty thousand and take the game's colour language away from them to do it - which is
  the sort of thing a settings row must not do either.

### Why no colour moved, with the numbers so nobody relitigates it
The shipped palette **passes all 84 promised pairs**, and the two thinnest are exactly the pairs you
would guess matter most: `enemyShot / shard` at **1.12** (protanopia, both axes) and
`enemyShot / playerShot` at **1.20** (greyscale). Deepening the enemy shot was the obvious candidate
- it is the palest warm thing in the game - and it is a trap: at `#ff8a45` that pair does go up to
1.41, but the shot lands **0.25** from the spitter's own body (it is 0.53 today) and 0.48 from a
bomber's blast, because "deeper warm" is where all the crowd's colours already live. The shot's
paleness is not an oversight; it is the one warm that no body wears, and its near-white core is what
makes it read as hot. Left alone on purpose, and the audit is the reason anybody can say so.

### What the audit did find, and left for a later session
Four pairs of *bodies* are under a step apart even for an eye with every cone: `darter / swarmling`
**0.35**, `swarmling / sniper` 0.76, `bomber / swarmling` 0.87, `spitter / bomber` 0.92. They are
tolerated because the three smallest bodies in the game (`weaver`, `darter`, `swarmling`) all get a
**dart silhouette** from `render/entities.js` while their sizes are 10/11/7 px and their colours are
three reds - so it is *shape* that is short here, which is precisely the other word in PLAN's
sentence. `test/palette-read.test.mjs` pins that list of four in `the crowd shares colours, and says
which pairs do`: it cannot get worse unnoticed, and the day somebody gives the swarmling its own
silhouette the list shortens and that is a better game.

### Things that bit, worth remembering
- **`node --test test` is not `node --test`.** The former looks for a *file* called `test` and dies
  with MODULE_NOT_FOUND; the suite is run from the root with no argument (that is what
  `package.json` and `tools/release.sh` both do).
- `core/palette.js`'s `parseColor` takes a *string* - `'#58ffa1'` or `'rgb(94,247,255)'` - and throws
  on anything else, loudly. It does not accept an already-parsed triple: a test that hands it `SKY`
  gets `not a colour this can read: 5,12,30`, which is the parser being exactly as strict as it
  should be. `tools/sights.js`'s `measure()` is the one that takes a sight and returns Oklab.
- The eyes are a **projection**, so "this eye is blind to this axis" means *zero*, not *small*: two
  colours that differ only along a lost axis score 0.00, not 0.05. That is why the STEP-based bars are
  per-axis maxima rather than a Euclidean distance - and why a wrongly wired eye is a silent pass
  rather than a loud fail, which is why it got a test.
- The report sorts by *margin*, so a clean run prints only the pairs within 0.45 of their bar; asking
  for `--all` when everything passes looks alarming and is not.

### What should come next
1. **The settings row** is the rest of milestone 9's colour-blind item. Decide first what a second
   step would *do*, because a row with one choice is a stub and the audit says the shipped palette
   does not need rescuing: the honest shapes are (a) a `MARKS` row that adds a shape or brightness
   signature to harm and help on top of the palette (which the audit's "shown, not promised" column is
   begging for, and which cannot break warm/cool because it does not touch hue), or (b) a full second
   scheme - ~30 colours, cards included, every one of them measured with `tools/palette-check.js`
   before it ships. (a) is the one that fits a session; (b) fits a milestone.
2. Then milestone 9's release checklist. Then still owed from earlier sessions: the **shot-speed
   line** (`tools/line-ab.js --line bulletSpeed --weapon pulse --seeds 1-16`), the **difficulty band**
   `tools/difficulty-arc.js` still fails, `tools/gun-tune.js` from session 96, session 101's
   **`--paint` door** on `tools/alloc-probe.js`, and milestone 10's browser half of the performance
   pass - then `1.0.0`.
3. Small things this session noticed and did not do: `cageWall` is so desaturated (`C` 0.053) that a
   protanope sees it **0.13** from the ship itself - harmless, because a cage cannot be mistaken for
   the ship you are piloting, and that is exactly the pair the promise matrix declines to judge, but
   it is a thin wall. And the audit has no opinion on the interface (cards, HUD, codex); a
   `tools/contrast-check.js` for text-on-panel would be the same ruler pointed at `render/cards.js`.

## Session 110 — A second signature over the palette: the MARKS row, measured at its faintest

Suite **1957 → 1970** (7 in `test/marks-art.test.mjs`, 6 in `test/palette-read.test.mjs`). The reference
run (`--seed 20261006 --trace`) is byte for byte session 109's again (10m00s / 73,982 / level 57 /
3,934 kills / 4,934 shards, 7 vacuums, 2036 in) - and the settings test now plays one seed twice with
**every picture row at both ends of its travel including `marks: full`** and asks for the same run, so the
new row is proven cosmetic in the same sentence the other four are.

Milestone 9's colour-blind item is ticked and released as **0.10.16**: session 109's measurement said the
shipped palette needs no rescuing, and the honest half that was left was the row.

### What landed
- **`MARKS` is the fifth picture row** on the settings panel: `FULL` / `FAINT` / `OFF`, shipping at
  `off`. It is the one row in the game that *adds* something rather than turning something down, so its
  steps run the other way from every other row here - `off` is the last step because the last step of
  every row is the game as it shipped, and a hand that keeps pressing `←` walks *up* the marks.
  `game/settings.js` says that in the row's own comment and `test/settings.test.mjs` walks it both ways.
- **What it paints** (`render/entities.js`): every enemy shot gets a dark centre punched through its hot
  core (`MARK_PUPIL_RATIO` 0.42 of the shot's own reach, which leaves a ring of light rather than a black
  disc with a halo) and every shard - either size - gets a lit spark set in its middle (0.42 of the body,
  inside the shard's own fading). Two palette colours, `markPupil` `#160b04` and `markCore` `#f2fff8`,
  neither of which has a hue worth the name: **a mark is light and the lack of it**, so it can be laid on
  top of anything the arena already wears without moving a body off warm-is-harm (there is a test named
  `a mark is a shade and not a colour`, and it allows four degrees of hue). The strength is written into
  the rgba and not into `globalAlpha`, because the entity pass already has a `globalAlpha` of 0.8 in
  flight and the two would multiply into something nobody chose.
- **Only the two small fast things are marked.** A crowd body has a silhouette, a size and a way of
  walking; a beam is a band of light nothing can be mistaken for; a wall is where the wall is; and the
  ship's own shot is already the lit half of the pair. That is the same argument the promise matrix makes
  about shape, and both halves of it are held: `test/marks-art.test.mjs` counts fills and proves the ship,
  its own gun and the whole crowd cost exactly what they cost with the row off, and
  `test/palette-read.test.mjs` asserts `markFor()` answers null for every one of them.
- **`tools/sights.js` grew the marks half**: `MARKS` (the two marks and which sights they paint, decided
  off `meaning` and `form` so a new dot-shaped harm is marked the day it is added), `marked(sight, share)`
  (the sight's colour with the mark blended over it by `ratio²`, i.e. the area the mark actually covers -
  deliberately harsh, since an eye that can resolve the shape gets more than that), and `auditMarks()`
  which reads the row's own steps out of `game/settings.js` and measures each one against every promise
  the palette makes.
- **Three promises about the marks**, all in `test/palette-read.test.mjs`: every step clears every
  promised pair *and* stays visible on the sky; every pair the palette promises a whole step of
  **brightness** about - the promise that says "shape is not enough here" - and that a mark touches, comes
  out further over its bar; and `enemyShot / shard` and `enemyShot / playerShot`, the two thinnest pairs
  in the shipped palette, each gain at least 0.4 of a step for an eye with no hue at the *faint* step. The
  full step buys about twice that: 1.12 → 2.49 and 1.20 → 2.57.
- **`tools/palette-check.js` prints a `When MARKS is asked for` section** and `--strict` fails on a mark
  that broke a promise, so the report and the tests cannot disagree - they call the same `auditMarks()`.

### What bit, in order of how much it wasted
1. **An edit that silently did half of what was asked.** One `edit` call with two hunks: the second hunk's
   `oldText` did not match, so the tool applied *nothing*, and I did not notice for a while - the constants
   and the shard half were in and the shot half was not, and `node --check` was happy the whole time. The
   art test found it ("one fill more than the same shot wore unmarked: 0 !== 1"), which is the first time
   this suite has caught a *missing feature* rather than a wrong value. Lesson: after a rejected multi-hunk
   edit, re-read the file before writing the next one.
2. **Two harness indices that hard-coded where the panel prints its rows.** Adding a fifth row shifted
   `MUSIC` from 5 to 6 and `AUTO-FIRE` from 8 to 9 in `test/volume.test.mjs` and `test/assists.test.mjs`
   (both now walk one further and read one further), and it broke the *writing* visit in a way that looked
   like a broken game: `tools/headless/text.js` pressed `ArrowDown` four times - a counted walk its own
   comment claimed it was not doing - landed the cursor on `MARKS` instead of the `KEYS` door, stepped the
   row instead of opening the rack, and then its two `O` presses left the panel up, so the visit never
   launched: `cards-not-dealt`, `win-not-reached`, and `test/words.test.mjs` red. It now walks down until
   the panel says the door is the row it is on. **`test/keys.test.mjs` had the same disease** and I only
   found it by running the whole suite: it asserted the settings cursor came back to row 4 where the door
   is now 5; it asks `doorRow()` now. Anything that walks a rack should ask where the rack printed the
   thing it is looking for.
3. **A shard planted next to the ship is not there by the time the frame is painted** - the magnet takes it
   (game/pickups.js, 145 px). The art test plants them 400 px out and pins their velocity, and reads the
   mark by its ink rather than its position, because a shard's mark is drawn inside the shard's own
   translate-and-rotate so the coordinates it was asked with are the shard's and not the arena's.
4. The harness's `circles()` logged no colour at all - so `arc` now records `fill`, `stroke` and `alpha`
   alongside `mode`. That is what lets a test say "the pupil was painted in `PALETTE.markPupil` at the
   row's share" instead of counting fills and hoping.

### Decisions, so nobody relitigates them
- **A mark may trade a hair of an axis an eye did not need for a lot of the one it did.** Marked
  `enemyShot / playerShot` goes 1.20 → 1.61 for a hueless eye and 2.59 → 2.36 for a red-green one, because
  a pupil takes a little warmth out of a warm dot and that eye was already 1.6 clear of its bar. The test
  asserts the pair's *margin* and the hueless gain, and the "every step clears every promise" test is what
  bounds the trade.
- **The audit measures a mark as an area-weighted mean and says so.** It is a floor, not a ceiling: a pupil
  covers about 18% of the shot's read area, and the picture an eye actually gets is a hole in a light,
  which anything with acuity reads as a shape. Anyone tempted to make the number prettier should notice
  that the *faint* step is what has to clear the bar, and it clears it by half a step.
- **`MARK_FAINT` is 0.45 of an opacity, not a smaller dot**: the faint step is the same picture with less
  ink in it, which is what makes it a *step* of one row rather than a different picture.
- The row has no key of its own and is not on the title's key line: it lives inside `O` like the other four
  picture rows, and the panel prints it.

### What should come next
1. Milestone 9's last item is its **release** - the milestone's checklist is that item; read it against
   what exists, tick it or argue with it. Then milestone 10's browser half of the performance pass,
   and `1.0.0`.
2. Still owed from earlier sessions: the **shot-speed line** (`tools/line-ab.js --line bulletSpeed
   --weapon pulse --seeds 1-16`), the **difficulty band** (`tools/difficulty-arc.js` still fails),
   `tools/gun-tune.js` from session 96, and session 101's `--paint` door on `tools/alloc-probe.js`.
3. Small things this session noticed and did not do: the audit still has no opinion on the **interface** (a
   `tools/contrast-check.js` pointed at `render/cards.js` text-on-panel would be the same ruler, and a
   third mark could serve the HUD); `cageWall` is still a thin wall for a protanope (0.13 from the ship,
   and deliberately unjudged); and the four crowd pairs that share a colour (`darter/swarmling` 0.35 above
   all) want a silhouette rather than a colour - which is the other word in PLAN's sentence and a different
   session.

## Session 111 — The owner's hangar hotfix: a panel puts the page underneath it to bed

Suite **1970 → 1982** (7 in `test/panel-aside.test.mjs`, 1 in `test/logo-calm.test.mjs`). The reference run
(`--seed 20261006 --trace`) is byte for byte session 110's again (10m00s / 73,982 / level 57 / 3,934 kills
/ 4,934 shards, 7 vacuums, 2036 in) - nothing in `game/` was touched. Released **0.10.17**.

`OVERLORDS_REQUESTS` arrived with a BUG-HOTFIX in it: *"The Hangar works fine, but due to insufficient
opacity, the root menu shines through... The main menu should not be visible at all from the hangar, or
perhaps just a slight, slight hint."* Bugs first, so this was the session. The entry is now in
`archive/COMPLETED_OVERLORDS_REQUESTS` with the note on what shipped.

### What landed
- **`ui/screens.js` `putScreensToBed(down)`** - the whole feature in four lines. `raisePanel` puts the
  three menu screens (title, wreck's card, win's card - `beds`, built beside `panels` in `initScreens`)
  to bed; `closePanels` lets them up. The page carries a new class, `aside`, and `index.html` gives it
  `opacity: .1` - written *above* `.screen.hidden` deliberately, because both rules say `opacity`, they
  are equally specific, and a screen can be both: `.hidden` has to be the one that wins. That precedence
  is a test and not a comment.
- **`render/logo.js` `dimLogo(on)` / `logoDim()`** - the other half of the title. The mark is painted on
  the canvas, so fading the page left the word glowing behind the hangar at full tube on its own. `dim`
  eases toward its target on the frame's clock inside `advanceLogo` (`DIM` 0.18, `DIM_FADE` 0.25 s, and
  it eases even after the arrival has finished, because a panel can be opened an hour into a page) and
  `drawLogo` stamps it once with `ctx.globalAlpha = dim` inside its `save` - one line covers the letters,
  the rule, the studs and the falling star, and `paintGlow` already multiplies the alpha it finds.
- **`main.js`** asks `dimLogo(panelIsUp())` on every frame, next to `advanceLogo`. Not on each open/close
  path: there are half a dozen of those and the mark only needs the answer once per frame.
- **What the eye gets, in numbers.** Before: the title's words came through the hangar's centre at 45% and
  the mark at 45%. After: the words are at 0.1 × 0.45 = **4.5%**, the mark at 0.18 × 0.45 = **8%**, and the
  arena behind them at 44% instead of 34% - the title's own veil went to a tenth with its words, so the
  crowd behind the hangar is a shade *clearer* than it was, dimmed once instead of twice. That is the
  "slight, slight hint" the request asked for, and it is why a bigger panel dim was not the answer: a dim
  strong enough to bury a page of bright type would have buried the arena too, and the arena behind the
  glass is the one thing these panels share with the pause.
- **A tenth and not nothing, on purpose.** `opacity` and not `.hidden` so it travels on the page's own
  0.28 s fade instead of blinking, and a tenth left behind so the hangar is still a window onto the arena
  rather than a card pasted on black. `prefers-reduced-motion` gets the change on one frame (the test in
  `logo-calm.test.mjs`), which is what that request means everywhere else in the game.
- **Harness** (`tools/headless/harness.js`): `classes(id)` beside `text(id)` (a test can ask which classes
  a screen ended up with instead of betting on one), the stroke log now records the `globalAlpha` each
  stroke was asked for and `measure()` hands it back as `alphas` - the only way in here to tell a dimmed
  mark from a missing one, since both cost the same strokes.

### The stub was the bug, not the game
The new art test went red first with a stroke at `0.0258` where everything else was at `0.18` - and it was
the *rig* that was wrong, and had been for a long time: the canvas stub's `save`/`restore` only gave the
transform back, so `paintGlow`'s `globalAlpha *= strength` leaked onto every stroke drawn after a glow
stamp in the same frame. No `src/` code was wrong (a real canvas restores alpha), but any test that read a
logged `alpha` after a stamp had been measured against a lying canvas. `save` now stacks
`{m, a, c}` - transform, alpha, composite - and the whole suite says the change is free.

### The orphan in the tree
`test/shot-speed.test.mjs` was sitting there **uncommitted** at session start - the shot-speed line the
last six sessions' notes kept listing as owed, apparently written by a session that ended before it could
verify it. It is complete, honest and passing: it measures the card on the world (a shot's `life` is a
fuse in seconds, so a rank buys `speed × life` of reach; a faster shot falls behind a walking body by
exactly the walk it saves; and the honest negative - the crowd walks into the reach a plain shot already
had, which is *why* `tools/line-ab.js` reads 1.00x on the pulse). Committed as its own commit after
`node --check` and a green run. **That closes the shot-speed item** - on the world, which is the only
place the effect is measurable at all, and it says so in its header comment.

### Decisions, so nobody relitigates them
- **Every menu screen goes, hidden or not.** `putScreensToBed` does not check `.hidden` first: a hidden
  screen wearing `aside` is a screen nobody can see, and the alternative is a branch that has to be
  remembered every time a screen is added. The CSS precedence is the guard, and it is tested.
- **The mark is dimmed and not hidden.** "Not visible at all" was the owner's first preference; a faint
  mark is the second, and it is the one that keeps the hangar inside the same place the title is. A mark
  that vanished outright would be a hole in the middle of the panel's glow.
- **`beds` does not include the panels themselves**, and the pause is not a bed: a held run is the subject
  of the pause panel, not a page underneath it.
- **The HUD behind the pause is the same shape of problem and was left alone.** `render/hud.js` is drawn
  while paused (score top-left, clock, hull pips) and comes through at 45% the way the menu did - but it
  sits at the edges, the pause panel is centred, and the pause's own headline already prints the two
  numbers that overlap most. Nobody has reported it; if it is ever done, it is `dimHud(world.paused)` and
  the same one line in `drawHUD`, not a stronger panel.
- **`dimLogo` is a request and `dim` is the state**, which is what keeps the calm-motion snap in one place
  instead of three callers each deciding whether to fade.

### What should come next
1. **Milestone 9's last item is still `- [ ] Release.`** (PLAN, end of M9). Session 110's note: read the
   milestone's checklist against what exists, tick it or argue with it. Whatever it turns out to be, that
   is the next session's one thing.
2. Then milestone 10: the **difficulty band** (`tools/difficulty-arc.js` still fails), `tools/gun-tune.js`
   from session 96, session 101's **`--paint` door** on `tools/alloc-probe.js`, the browser half of the
   performance pass - and `1.0.0`. The **shot-speed line is done** (see the orphan above).
3. Still owed from session 110 and unchanged: an interface half of the colour audit (`tools/contrast-check.js`
   aimed at `render/cards.js` text-on-panel), `cageWall` is a thin wall for a protanope (0.13 from the ship,
   deliberately unjudged), and the four crowd pairs that share a colour (`darter`/`swarmling` 0.35 above all)
   want a silhouette rather than a colour.

## Session 112 — The palette's shapes are read out of the renderer now. Released **0.10.18**, which closes milestone 9

Suite **1982 → 1985** (3 in `test/palette-read.test.mjs`); the reference run (`--seed 20261006 --trace`)
is byte for byte session 111's again (10m00s / 73,982 / level 57 / 3,934 kills / 4,934 shards, 7 vacuums,
2036 in), which it must be, since the only `src/` edits were comments and one named constant.

Milestone 9's last item was `- [ ] Release.`. It is ticked (PLAN now says 0.9.0 - 0.10.18 is that
milestone) and 0.10.18 is out. But a release of nothing would have been a lie of a different shape,
because reading the milestone's colour item back against the tree is what found the bug below.

### What landed
- **`tools/sights.js`'s form table was wrong, and about the one thing it was there to be honest
  about.** It called the weaver, the darter and the swarmling three `dart`s. `render/entities.js`'s
  branch in `drawEnemy` gives the darter its own `dartPath` and gives the other two `shipPath` - the
  generic pointed-ship silhouette the game paints its own ships with, the weaver at spike 1.7 and the
  swarmling at 2.1. Session 109 wrote that table by eye; the file's own doc comment, four lines above
  the table, already said "render/entities.js gives the weaver a ship silhouette, the darter a dart"
  and the table contradicted it. The sizes were pinned against the renderer's source and the forms
  were not, so the sizes were never wrong and the forms were.
- **`BODY_FORMS` is now exported and pinned**: `the silhouettes the table measures are the silhouettes
  the renderer draws` opens `src/render/entities.js`, matches
  `/enemy\.type === '(\w+)'\)\s+(\w+)\(/g` (only the five silhouette branches answer to it - the four
  other `enemy.type ===` tests in the file are followed by a block and not a call), translates each
  path function through `PATH_FORMS`, falls back to `POLYGON_FORMS[sides]` for whatever reaches the
  `else polygon(...)`, and fails the table on any disagreement. It also asserts the `else polygon`
  line is still there, so a rearranged branch is loud instead of quietly measuring nothing.
- **The corrected promise**: `swarmling / ship` and `weaver / ship` are one form, so `howMuch` calls
  them alike and asks for a whole step on every axis an eye keeps - previously the swarmling's pair with
  the ship was asked for 0.55 of hue and nothing of brightness. Both clear it: **swarmling 2.49, weaver
  1.77**, same on the red-green eyes and on the eye with no hue. Nothing was repainted, and now the
  reason is a measurement instead of a shrug.
- **`sharedSilhouettes()`** groups the crowd by form and, for each pair inside a group, reports the
  size ratio, the colour separation with the worst eye named, and `carriedBy`: `colour`, `size`, `both`
  or `nothing`. The rule it enforces is one sentence: **two bodies of one shape, one size and one colour
  are one body, whoever painted them** - so a shared silhouette must be paid for by a step of colour or
  by more than `SAME_SIZE_RATIO` of size. Today there is one shared pair, `weaver / swarmling` at 1.43x
  apart in size and 0.72 of a step in colour: size carries it, colour does not, and that is the honest
  description of what session 109 left as "the crowd shares colours".
- **`shipBorrowers()`** is the same question aimed at the one sharing that can cost a run - a warm body
  wearing your own shape, coming at you - and `palette-check.js` prints a *Who shares a silhouette*
  section with both halves in it. `--strict` now exits non-zero on an unpaid shared silhouette as well
  as on a broken colour promise, so the section is a guard and not decoration.
- **`WEAVER_SPIKE = 1.7` named** in `render/entities.js` beside `SWARM_SPIKE`, because two lines that
  both borrow the ship's silhouette should look like it in the source and not only in a comment. The
  two balance rows that said "drawn as a long thin dart" (which is the loose wording that caused the
  whole thing) now say what is drawn: the ship's pointed silhouette, nose pulled out.

### The art decision this session did *not* make, and why
Four sessions of notes have said "the crowd's small bodies want a silhouette rather than a colour". The
corrected measurement says the harm-vs-help and harm-vs-self confusions - the only ones that cost a run -
are already paid for, by a whole step, on every eye. What is left is two harms that are 0.72 of a step
apart and 1.43x apart in size, which PLAN hands to shape, size and motion and which the audit deliberately
does not promise. So a new silhouette for the swarmling would be an art job for its own sake, and the one
thing I cannot check from here is the one thing an art job is: whether it reads. The crowd's most numerous
body, painted blind, on a geometry argument, is how this game gets worse. **Decision: nobody repaints the
swarmling from a headless session.** The audit now says precisely which pairs lean on size alone, so a
session with eyes on a screen has something to repaint *against*; the pinned list in
`test/palette-read.test.mjs` is what shortens when that happens.

### Things that bit
- **The edit tool's all-or-nothing multi-hunk behaviour bit again** (session 110's note). One call, two
  hunks on `balance.js`, the first one's `oldText` did not match (I had the `color:` line two rows too
  early), so *nothing* was applied. `git diff --stat` before writing anything more is the whole remedy
  and it costs one second.
- **A report function that `return`s nothing on its clean path** would have made the verdict print `NaN
  measurements under the bar`: `reportForms()` returned early with no value when nothing was shared and
  the caller added that to the failure count. Fixed with `return 0`. Worth remembering for every
  counting function added to this report - `NaN` is a lie of silence, and the verdict line is the only
  thing a busy reader looks at.
- **Every new guard was falsified before it was trusted**, and it is the cheapest useful minute in this
  project: `BODY_FORMS.weaver` put back to `'dart'` turned two tests red (the parse test, and the pinned
  group list); `SAME_SIZE_RATIO` and `FULL` both set to 99 made the report print `NEITHER of them
  carries it` and 238 failures, which is the unpaid path and the `--strict` hook actually working.
- **A test name with an apostrophe in it needs double quotes** - `test('what wears the ship's own
  silhouette...', ...)` is a syntax error, and `node --check` says so immediately, which is the only
  reason it took one run.
- `tools/` still may not import `src/render/`, which is why the forms and sizes are written down twice
  and pinned by reading source text. A third copy of anything drawn would be the point to revisit that
  rule, not to add another `readFileSync`.

### Decisions worth keeping
- **How the parse could go quietly wrong**: it looks for `enemy.type === 'kind') somePath(`. If a future
  session chooses silhouettes another way - a per-kind map, a lookup table, a data file - the regex
  finds nothing and the `drawn.size >= 4` assertion is what shouts. A rearrangement is loud; a new
  mechanism has to be met by rewriting this test, and that is the intended cost.
