### What shipped
- **`SETTINGS` is the fourth chip on the title rail.** It used to be refused because "a chip that opened a
  page a finger could neither use nor leave would be a trap". The panel now answers a tap, so the bar is met.
  The rail's CSS gained `flex-wrap: wrap` - four chips do not fit across a 375 px phone - which is the one
  thing in this session I could not look at.
- **A press on a settings row is answered by the row.** `ui/chips.js` grew `settingRowAt(x, y)`, which asks
  the browser where each row of `#settingRow` came to rest and answers which one the press landed on - the
  same arithmetic as a chip, against the same box the eye read. `main.js` `pressSettingsPanel` says what it
  means. A panel that is not up is `display: none`, so its rows have no boxes and answer nothing; no flag
  needed.
- **A `CLOSE` chip stands on the panel** (`.settings .chip`, inside the fitted column like the pause's GIVE
  UP), and it is `onSettings` - the very `O` toggle, guards and re-raising the pause included. It is put away
  for a visit with no fingers, which has the letter.
- **The two lines under the rows are written for the hand that arrived**: `ui/screens.js`
  `paintSettingsHints(hasFinger)`, once per visit beside `showChips` and `paintLaunchHints`, on the same fact.
  A thumb reads `TAP A ROW TO CHANGE IT`; the line naming `O`, `Esc`, `M` and `[ ] - =` is taken away
  (`.keys.gone`, a new rule - `.keys .gone` only ever took a *clause* out of a line).

### The thing that nearly got built wrong, and why it is worth writing down
The obvious rule - *a tap on a row is what the right arrow does* - would have shipped a **dead panel**. Most
of these rows ship at the top of their travel: `stepRow` deliberately does not wrap (game/settings.js says
why: "a key that comes back round to the beginning is a key that can put the shake back on while you were
trying to take it off"), and `SCREEN SHAKE`, `HIT FLASH`, `PARTICLES` and both sliders all start at their
last step. So `+1` answers nothing on them. Worse, the two switches a phone player most wants at that panel -
AUTO-FIRE and AUTO-AIM - are **on** for a run flown on a thumb, so `+1` answers nothing on those either. A
thumb would have tapped eight of ten rows and watched nothing move.

So a row now carries a second verb beside `step`: **`cycle`, the row's next value coming back round to its
first**, answered by whoever owns the table - `cycleRow` in game/settings.js (the only wrap in the game, with
the reason beside it), the sliders wrapped through their own door (`music(1) || music(-VOLUME.steps)`), the
two switches flipped, the mute as it already was. The arrow keys keep their no-wrapping rule untouched. A tap
is a different gesture: one press, on one row, whose word is on the glass in front of the player.

### `hasKeyboard()`, and the trap it closes
The KEYS row is a *door* onto the controls rack, and every verb in that rack is a key press. A phone that
opens it can enter and cannot leave - the rack has no chip and answers no press. So the row is painted only
for a visit that has **ever pressed a key** (`input/keyboard.js`, sticky, re-exported through `input/index.js`).

Why not `hasFinger()`: a touchscreen laptop answers that yes while holding a keyboard, and nothing in a
browser says whether a keyboard is plugged in. A visit that has pressed a key has a keyboard - that is not an
inference, it is the press. The cost is one corner of a corner: a touchscreen laptop that taps SETTINGS before
touching a key sees the row appear on the panel's next repaint.

### A drift bug found while writing the tests
`settingRows()` was being rebuilt on every press as well as every paint, and the two can disagree: the first
key press of a visit turns the KEYS row on, a key press does not repaint the panel, and the freshly built
list is then **one row longer than the glass says it is** - a tap on the eighth row an eye can see steps the
ninth. Fixed by keeping `paintedRows`, the list exactly as last printed, and having the taps, the arrows and
the cursor all walk that. The row objects still ask their owners live for their words and their steps; what is
kept is only the shape that was printed.

### The harness grew a layout for rows
`document.createElement` rows had **no `getBoundingClientRect` at all** in the stub - a press hit-test against
a rack row would have thrown. `makeElement` now carries a `rect` slot answering a zero box (which
`landedOn` rightly refuses to press), and the controller grew `layOutRows(id, boxes)`: a test says where the
browser laid the rows out, after the panel has been painted, because rows have no id to be named by. This is
the piece the codex and the hangar will want next.

### Two wrong tests, both worth keeping in mind
1. I asserted AUTO-FIRE reads `ON` on a phone visit's title screen. It reads `OFF`: `game/assists.js` answers
   for the hand the run is *being flown on*, and `input/touch.js` `thumbUsed()` is honest that a screen tap is
   not a control claim. The test now walks `OFF -> ON -> OFF`, which exercises the wrap anyway.
2. I asserted the SETTINGS chip closes the panel it opened. It does not, and it was already right not to: a
   panel owns the glass it is up on, chips included (`test/thumb-rail.test.mjs` has held that for MUTE since
   session 123). The way out is the chip standing *on* the panel.

And a real one: my boot edit lost the `paintSettingsHints(hasFinger())` call - the comment survived and the
call did not - and the new test caught it as an empty line. Re-read the diff, not just the intent.

### Verified
18 new tests, all reading the **owners** (`pictureWords('shake')`, `isMuted()`, `musicLevel()`,
`assistWords('fire')`) and not just the panel's words. Mutation-checked: replacing `cyclePictureRow` with
`stepPictureRow(id, 1)` reddens two. Full suite green, `tools/simulate.js` unchanged, released as **v1.7.0**.

### What should come next
1. **The hangar's thumb shape** - the one that costs the player something. A phone visitor earns stardust all
   run and cannot spend a coin of it: `H` has no chip, the rack is picked by number keys, and buying is a
   Shift-chord. Decide: does a chip open the hangar from the title rail (it is a *reading* panel, which is the
   reason it was left off), does a tap on a row mean *buy* (and what stops a careless tap spending the purse),
   and does the ship rack answer a tap the way `1-9` does. `layOutRows` and `settingRowAt`'s shape are ready
   for it; `test/settings-rows-mouse.test.mjs` is the pattern for the no-finger half.
2. **The codex's thumb shape**, same family and cheaper: it only reads, so it wants a chip, rows that can be
   walked by a tap, and a way out.
3. **The once-per-screen audit's guard half**, unchanged from 124-126: give the harness's `makeElement` a write
   counter (`domWrites()`) and hold that a settled screen writes nothing per frame.
4. **Make the harness send events the way a real browser does** (from session 127): both names, and sometimes
   only one.
5. Still owed, unchanged: the browser half of the performance pass (a THICK CROWD run standing 150 bodies on a
   scheduled run), `tools/gun-tune.js`, `cageWall` as a thin wall for a protanope, silhouettes for the crowd
   pairs that share a colour, the afterimage's flat top of the ladder, and the deliberate FAIL on the
   difficulty band (13% of 48 seeds die between 4 m and 9 m against the 50% "usually" asks for).

## Session 129 — The shop answers a thumb: the HANGAR chip, and a row that asks before it takes the purse. Released **1.8.0**

### What shipped
A phone visitor has been earning stardust for every run of every visit and could not spend a coin of it: the
shop opens with `H`, its ships are picked with number keys, and buying is a `SHIFT + digit` chord. Now:

* `HANGAR` is the **fifth chip** on the thumb rail, and `hangarClose` is the second chip standing *on* a panel.
* A tap on a **bought ship row** is the number key: the next run flies it, free, lit by the same `showShip`.
* A row that **costs stardust asks**. First tap: `TAP AGAIN TO BUY IT` in the row's own price line, warm amber.
  Second tap on that row: the purchase. Another row, the glass between the rows, and the way out all take it
  off, and it never outlives the panel.
* A cursor gets the same two taps and the row says `CLICK AGAIN TO BUY IT`.

### The ask is the shape
Buying is the only press in the game that takes something from the purse, and a finger has no chord to lean on.
So the confirmation did not move into a dialog or a second screen — it moved into the row that was already
printing the price. Three things make that safe and all three are tested: the ask is only ever put on a row the
purse could actually pay for (`game/hangar.js` `priceAt` answers "what would this row cost, or is there nothing
to sell"), it is cancelled by every other press, and it is forgotten when the panel goes down. A purse too short
is a **silent press**: the shop does not ask a question it already knows the answer to.

`buyWords` in `ui/screens.js` is where the two hands part: the price is always first and always stays (the rule
that money only moves while the price is on the glass predates this), and only the second clause changes —
`SHIFT + 2 BUYS IT` for a hand with keys, `TAP TO BUY IT` / `TAP AGAIN TO BUY IT` for a finger, `CLICK AGAIN
TO BUY IT` for a cursor that took the two taps.

### `PANEL_CHIPS`, so there is one fact and not two
`showSettingsClose`/`settingsCloseAt` became `showPanelChips`/`panelChipAt(which, x, y)` over a list of the chips
that stand on panels. One fact puts them up (`hasFinger`, once per visit) and one question gets asked of them
(did this press land on *this* panel's way out). The awards rack is deliberately not among the pressable lists:
it sells nothing, so a press on an award row is a press on a line of words.

### Two real bugs the tests found, both in code that had been shipped for a while
1. **`openRack` never repainted the racks.** Ownership only ever changed through `buyFromRack`, which repaints,
   so nothing had ever been seen stale — but the ask lives in the same rows, and a shop that came back up had
   the previous visit's row still lit amber. `openRack` now clears the ask and paints both racks from their
   owners on the way up, which is what the doc above those functions always claimed they did.
2. **The `CHIPS` array never got the hangar entry** even though `index.html` and the harness both had the chip.
   The tap fell through to the title's click-to-launch and started a run. Caught by the second test of the new
   file, which asserts the tap does *not* launch.

### One test bug worth remembering
The tests in a file share one world, and **purchases persist across `resetToTitle`** (as they should — it is the
save). A test that bought ship 2 left every later test's ship 2 bought, which turned an "ask" into a "pick" and
sent me hunting through the wrong functions. Each test now uses its own row. The general lesson for the codex
file: `resetToTitle` resets the *run*, not the *visit*.

I also lost an hour to stdout ordering: `node --test` does not guarantee that a `console.log` from the module
under test interleaves in real order with one from the test file. The "impossible" trace was two tests' logs
printed next to each other. Put the probe in the test, next to the assert, not in the code under test.

### Verified
18 new tests (`test/thumb-hangar.test.mjs` for the finger, `test/hangar-rows-mouse.test.mjs` for the cursor),
all reading the **owners** — `world.dust`, `world.ownedShips`, `world.perkRanks` via `perkLedger`, `priceOf` —
and not just the glass. Mutation-checked twice: dropping the `cost > world.dust` guard reddens exactly the
purse test; dropping `askingRow = NOT_ASKING` from `openRack` reddens three. Full suite **2322/2322**,
`tools/simulate.js --seed 20261006` traces the same fingerprint as before, released as **1.8.0**.

### What should come next
1. **The codex's thumb shape** — the last reading panel, and the cheapest of the three: it only reads, so it
   wants a chip, rows a tap can walk (its rows expand? decide whether a tap does anything at all beyond
   scrolling), and a way out. `layOutRows`, `rowAt` and `PANEL_CHIPS` are all ready for it. Decide honestly
   whether a codex row has a verb at all: if it has none, a chip plus a CLOSE chip may be the whole item, and
   the panel is scrollable, which is a thumb shape of its own.
2. **The once-per-screen audit's guard half**, unchanged from 124-126: give the harness's `makeElement` a write
   counter (`domWrites()`) and hold that a settled screen writes nothing per frame.
3. **Make the harness send events the way a real browser does** (from 127): both names, and sometimes only one.
4. Still owed, unchanged: the browser half of the performance pass (a THICK CROWD run standing 150 bodies on a
   scheduled run), `tools/gun-tune.js`, `cageWall` as a thin wall for a protanope, silhouettes for the crowd
   pairs that share a colour, the afterimage's flat top of the ladder, and the deliberate FAIL on the difficulty
   band (13% of 48 seeds die between 4 m and 9 m against the 50% "usually" asks for).

## Session 130 — The record turns a page: the CODEX chip, and five racks a thumb walks. Released **1.9.0**

### What shipped
The last panel a phone could not reach. It is also the only one with **no verb at all**: a codex row answers
no press in either hand, because there is nothing to do to a thing you have already met. So the thumb shape
here is not a press, it is a *shape* - the panel has to fit the window it is opened on.

* `CODEX` is the **sixth chip** on the rail.
* A thumb's record comes up on **one rack** - hosts - and two chips stand under it: `NEXT RACK` (walks the
  five, wraps) and `CLOSE` (is `C`, the same toggle).
* A keyboard visit sees all five at once, in the words the page ships, with no chips anywhere.

### Why paging and not scrolling
Five racks, forty-odd rows: side by side they fit a desktop; in a phone's width `.racks` wraps them into one
column roughly 1400px tall against a window of ~780. `fitPanel` scales a panel to fit with a floor of
`RACK_MIN` (0.6), and past the floor it simply overflows - the doc above `fitHangar` already says these
panels do not scroll and a rack that does not fit is a rack nobody sees. So the honest options were scroll or
page, and scrolling is not available: **every screen is `pointer-events: none`** and the press comes in
through the canvas, which is what makes a tap and a click one press in the first place. Turning that off for
one panel would put a second input path back into a game that spent sessions removing it. Paging is the shape
that keeps the one press handler.

### Where the page number lives
In `ui/screens.js`, not `main.js`. The codex is painted from **two doors** - the visit opening, and a run's
card landing (`showGameOver`/`showVictory` call `showCodex`, `showLog`, `showAwards`, `showRules`
themselves) - and if `main.js` held the page, the death's card would have been showing all five racks again
under a thumb. `paintCodexHints(onGlass)` sets `codexPaged` once per visit (it is the only once-per-visit
call about the codex), `openCodex` puts the page back to 0, and `turnCodexRack()` asks the panel to fit
itself again because one rack is a shorter column than five.

### `PANEL_CHIPS` grew a paint/press pair
The codex's two chips are laid side by side in a `.chip-row` that is hidden as a unit, but they are pressed
one at a time. So each entry now names `paint` (the box the page hides) and `press` (the box the press is
answered against) - the same element except here. `panelChipAt('codex', x, y)` is the CLOSE chip and
`panelChipAt('codexNext', x, y)` the turn.

### A style test caught a harness mistake, and it was right to
`test/words.test.mjs` walks **every string in the harness's screen snapshot** and holds that the interface
voice in it is caps. My first `codexShown` reported the racks as `['hosts', 'lines', ...]` and the test
failed on `"hosts"`. That is the guard doing its job: a test label had started to look like page copy. The
snapshot now reports the rack **titles** the player actually reads - `['HOSTS', 'CARD LINES', ...]` - which
is both legal under the voice rule and better in a test failure.

### One test of my own was wrong, and it was the interesting one
I asserted that tapping the shop's chip while the record is up opens the shop. It does not and must not: a
panel owns the glass it is up on, chips included. The test now says that out loud, then closes the record and
opens the shop - which is the actual navigation a phone has.

### Verified
13 new tests (`test/thumb-codex.test.mjs`, `test/codex-rows-mouse.test.mjs`). Mutation-checked: forcing
`codexPaged = false` reddens five. Full suite **2336/2336**, `tools/simulate.js --seed 20261006` traces the
same fingerprint, released as **1.9.0**.

### What should come next
1. **The once-per-screen audit's guard half**, owed since 124: give the harness's `makeElement` a write
   counter (`domWrites()`) and hold that a settled screen writes nothing per frame. Session 125 found a card
   painting itself sixty times a second by accident; nothing yet fails a test if that happens again.
2. **Make the harness send events the way a real browser does** (from 127): both `code` and `key`, and
   sometimes only one. The D-key fix is tested by hand; the harness still always sends the same shape.
3. **The thumb work is closed, so pick from the owed list**: the browser half of the performance pass (a
   THICK CROWD run standing 150 bodies on a scheduled run), `tools/gun-tune.js`, `cageWall` as a thin wall
   for a protanope, silhouettes for the crowd pairs that share a colour, the afterimage's flat top of the
   ladder, and the deliberate FAIL on the difficulty band (13% of 48 seeds die between 4 m and 9 m against
   the 50% "usually" asks for).

## Session 131 — The page is counted: `domWrites()`, and a settled screen held to zero. Not released (see below)

### What shipped
The guard half of the audit session 124 started and session 125 found the reason for. `tools/headless/harness.js`
now counts every write to the stub DOM, and `test/dom-writes.test.mjs` (8 tests) holds that each screen of the
game, once it has **settled**, writes nothing per frame: the title, the shop, the record, the settings, a run
being flown, the wreck's card, the pause, and the win's card.

### What counts as a write
Text put into an element (`textContent` is now an accessor on every stub element), a child added, a child taken
away. Not a class toggled to the value it already had - the real `classList.toggle` does nothing in that case
either, and counting it would make every panel look guilty. `game.domWrites()` reads the tally and
`game.resetDomWrites()` zeroes it, which is the part that makes the number mean anything: the boot writes the
whole page once, so a count that includes it would say everything is fine whatever happened afterwards.

### The control test is the one that matters
Six of the eight tests assert zero, and **a counter that counted nothing would pass all six.** So one test
puts the shop up and demands the count be *seen*, then measures the same settled page again and demands zero -
one screen, both answers, next to each other. Another reads the whole snapshot and steps a frame to hold that
*looking* at the page is not writing it, which is what stops the harness failing its own tests.

Mutation-checked against the historical bug: dropping `!overCardShown` from the death-card branch in `main.js`
(the exact thing session 125 fixed) reddens the wreck's-card test with **7260 writes against the 0 it asks
for**. The guard is not decorative.

### A fact worth having written down: a flying run writes the page zero times
I expected a run in motion to write its score and purse, and it writes nothing - the in-run HUD is painted on
the canvas with the fight (`render/hud.js`) and the DOM is only the screens *around* it. The test asserts the
zero anyway, with that said: the day any of that moves onto the page, this is the test that tells whoever
moved it that it has to be written when it changes and not once per frame.

### Why this was not released
Nothing a player can see or feel changed: the commit is the harness and a test file, and `releases/v1.9.0` is
already the identical playable build. A menu entry that plays the same as the one under it is noise. If a
future session ships something playable on top of this, it rides along in that release.

### Verified
Full suite **2345/2345**, `tools/simulate.js --seed 20261006` traces the same fingerprint as every session
since 127, and the mutation above.

### What should come next
1. **Make the harness send events the way a real browser does** (from 127): both `code` and `key`, sometimes
   only one. The D-key fix is only tested by hand today.
2. **The owed list, now that the thumb work is closed**: the browser half of the performance pass (a THICK
   CROWD run standing 150 bodies on a scheduled run), `tools/gun-tune.js`, `cageWall` as a thin wall for a
   protanope, silhouettes for the crowd pairs that share a colour, the afterimage's flat top of the ladder,
   and the deliberate FAIL on the difficulty band (13% of 48 seeds die between 4 m and 9 m against the 50%
   "usually" asks for).
3. **Something the new guard makes cheap**: the same measurement on a *live* screen - `domWrites()` per frame
   during a busy fight with 150 bodies - would turn "the page is quiet" into a number the performance pass
   can compare against instead of a rule it hopes is true.

## Session 132 — The harness sends a key the way a browser does. Not released (harness and tests only)

### What shipped
`game.key(code, down, extra)` now sends **both names a real key event carries**: `code` (the place) and `key`
(what that key prints). It used to send only the place - which meant that since session 127 shipped the
"hear the printing first" rule, **the entire suite of ~2300 tests was exercising the fallback half of the
keyboard** and calling it the primary one. Only `test/key-names.test.mjs`, which builds its own events, had
ever touched the path every player actually uses.

The suite went green unchanged. That is the result this change was for: the primary path is now the one
everything runs on, and it was already correct.

### The table is the harness's, not the game's
`PRINTED` in `tools/headless/harness.js` spells out what a US-layout browser prints for each place: letters,
digits, F1-F12, the arrows and the named keys, the punctuation, and the numpad. It is deliberately **not**
borrowed from `core/keymap.js`: a harness that asks the game what a key prints can only ever agree with it,
and the agreement would prove nothing.

An unknown code throws (`the harness has no printing for a key called Numpad99`) rather than sending an event
no browser could send. That caught one real case the same day: `test/ship-pick.test.mjs` presses `Numpad5`,
which the table did not have.

`events` on the boot takes a name away - `'place'` for the browser that reported no place (session 127's
tester), `'print'` for an input method that reports only the printing. Nothing uses those modes yet; they are
there so the two halves can be tested apart the day a test wants them.

### The guard that makes it worth having
`test/harness-events.test.mjs` (5 tests):
* the wire carries both names, and a chord carries `shiftKey` beside them;
* an unknown place is an error;
* **for every place the game can be bound to, the word the harness prints maps back to that same place**
  (`codeForWord(printedFor(code)) === code`) - if the two tables ever drift, the suite is silently back on
  the fallback and this says so;
* and the same from the other end, once per action the game offers.

Mutation-checked: printing `x` for `KeyD` reddens three of the five.

Two small honest notes the tests forced out: the game's own word for a key is a **legend for eyes** (`SPACE`,
`ESC`) and not the wire's (`' '`, `'Escape'`), so the spelling is only compared where the wire prints a
character. And the stub window had `addEventListener` but no `removeEventListener` - a listener list you
cannot take a handler out of leaks the test's own handler into every later event of the file.

### Verified
Full suite **2350/2350**, `tools/simulate.js --seed 20261006` unchanged. Not released: nothing a player can
see changed, and `releases/v1.9.0` is the same playable build (same call as session 131).

### What should come next
1. **The owed list**, now the input and thumb work are closed: the browser half of the performance pass (a
   THICK CROWD run standing 150 bodies on a scheduled run), `tools/gun-tune.js`, `cageWall` as a thin wall for
   a protanope, silhouettes for the crowd pairs that share a colour, the afterimage's flat top of the ladder,
   and the deliberate FAIL on the difficulty band (13% of 48 seeds die between 4 m and 9 m against the 50%
   "usually" asks for).
2. **Something the new guards make cheap**: `domWrites()` per frame during a busy 150-body fight, so the
   performance pass has a number for "the page is quiet" instead of a hope.
3. A thought worth writing down before someone rediscovers it: the harness now *is* a US layout. A test that
   wants a different one says so by hand, the way `key-names.test.mjs` does with its Dvorak-style event.

## Session 133 — The palette audit measures the two energy walls as they are painted. Not released (tools and tests only)

### The owed item turned out to be a measurement artefact, not a colour
`cageWall` has been on every session's owed list since 108: "a thin wall for a protanope, 0.13 from the
ship, deliberately unjudged". Measured properly it is **2.44 steps** from the ship on the red-green eyes -
nowhere near a problem. The 0.13 was an artefact.

`PALETTE.cageWall` is `#bfe9ff`, a near-white. It is never painted as a near-white: `render/boss.js` lays it
down at **62% over a near-black sky**, where it lands around `#7a99ad` - a mid grey-blue, far darker and far
greyer than the entry reads. `tools/sights.js` composites a *fill* over the sky before measuring it and says
so in its own doc ("A translucent colour is not a colour until it has been put on the thing behind it, so
every measurement composites first") - but it never composited a **line**. Every line in the table was
measured at full opacity. For the 40-odd bodies that is fine, because they are painted opaque. For the two
energy walls it is wrong by a mile.

### What changed
* `tools/sights.js`: a sight may carry `alpha`, the opacity it is painted at, and `measure()` composites the
  line over the sky when it does. Applied to `wall` (`LINE_LIGHT` 0.5, from `render/walls.js`) and `cage`
  (`CAGE_LINE_LIGHT` 0.62, from `render/boss.js`). Every other sight is unchanged, because every other sight
  is painted opaque - checked, not assumed: the bomber's zone ring and the mine's trigger ring are both drawn
  at `globalAlpha` near 1, so measuring them as written is right.
* `test/palette-read.test.mjs`: the two alphas are read out of the two renderers' source, the same way the
  shard/mine sizes already are, so a change in a renderer fails the audit's own test the day it happens. Plus
  a test that says the effect out loud: composited, the cage is more than a whole step further from the ship
  than it looked, and an eye with no red cone is handed a difference to see.
* `tools/palette-check.js`: the COLOUR column now says `#bfe9ff at 0.62 on the sky` for a sight measured
  composited, so a near-white hex is not printed beside a mid-grey measurement with no explanation.

All 84 promised pairs still pass. `ship / cage` fell out of the "pairs with nothing at stake, near zero"
shortlist on its own, which is the report telling the same story the tests now hold.

Mutation-checked: dropping `alpha` from the cage sight reddens both new tests.

### The part worth keeping in mind
A tool that measures the wrong thing does not fail - it **reports**, and the report gets read into the
notes and re-copied for twenty sessions. The number was never wrong; the question was. Before re-copying an
owed item, ask what was actually measured.

### Verified
Full suite **2352/2352**, `tools/simulate.js --seed 20261006` unchanged, `node tools/palette-check.js` clean.
Not released: nothing on the glass changed.

### What should come next
1. **The rest of the owed list**: the browser half of the performance pass (a THICK CROWD run standing 150
   bodies on a scheduled run), `tools/gun-tune.js`, silhouettes for the crowd pairs that share a colour, the
   afterimage's flat top of the ladder, and the deliberate FAIL on the difficulty band (13% of 48 seeds die
   between 4 m and 9 m against the 50% "usually" asks for).
2. **The same question for the other marks the audit makes**: `tools/sights.js` measures a shot by its body
   and promises nothing about its core, and measures a mark as an area-weighted mean. Both are stated and
   deliberate - but the alpha discovery suggests walking the whole table once and asking, for each row, "is
   this the colour an eye is handed?" `render/entities.js` has the answer for every one of them.
3. `domWrites()` per frame during a busy 150-body fight, so the performance pass has a number for "the page
   is quiet" instead of a hope.

### Addendum, same session: the walk continued, and one more row was measuring a colour nobody paints
Session 133's own "what should come next" asked whether every row of `tools/sights.js` is the colour an eye
is handed. Walked it against the renderers:

* **The sniper's beam was not.** `PALETTE.beamEdge` is measured as the band's line, but `bandPasses` paints
  the band's full width at `BAND_FILL` (0.3) and only the narrower middle at `BAND_HOT` (0.6), with a nearly
  white axis on top. The row declares the full width as its size, so it is now measured at 0.3 - the least of
  the three, which is the harsh and correct pairing of that size with that colour. All 84 promised pairs still
  pass at 0.3 (and did at 0.6, so this row was never carrying a promise on its translucency alone).
* **The crowd, the shots, the mine and the shard are fine.** Bodies are stroked opaque (`look.color`); the
  mine's shell and the bomber's thin ring are opaque; a shard's outline is `shardLine` but its glow - the
  biggest thing it paints, and the colour the row names - is `shard`, which is what the row measures.
* The test now also holds that **no other row claims an opacity the table has not checked against a
  renderer**, so a future row cannot quietly invent one.

Suite still **2352/2352**.

## Session 134 — `tools/gun-tune.js`, the knob session 96 asked for and never got. Not released (a tool and its tests)

### What it is
The throwaway session 96 measured thirty gun probes with, promoted to a file in the repo:

```
node tools/gun-tune.js --gun pulse --set fireRate=2.6
node tools/gun-tune.js --gun lance --sweep fireRate=1.3,2.6,5.2
node tools/gun-tune.js --gun swarm --sweep damage=1.25,1.5,2 --seeds 1-6 --seconds 600 --shards 6
```

It patches one field of a `BALANCE.weapons` row, plays the batch, and prints one row per condition
with the shipped row always first, on the same seeds, in the same process. `--set` patches are held
for every value of a sweep, so one table walks one axis. `--shards K` splits the seeds over child
processes the way `weapon-ladder` does.

### The flag it exists for is `--sweep`, not `--set`
Session 96's own lesson: *"a probe that 'does not fix it' has to say how far it probed."* That
session wrote "`damage` 5→3 with `fireRate` 0.9→1.4 gives 5,508 — no better" and concluded the rate
was not the lever. The rate was the lever; 1.4 was not far enough, because what a rate buys is
whether the press round the ship is thinned **at all**, which is a cliff and not a slope. A single
`--set` prints an answer with no axis next to it, so `--sweep` refuses fewer than two values.

Two traps the table points at rather than hides, both from that same session:
* moving `fireRate` moves the per-**pull** numbers with it (`recoil`, `knockback`, `muzzle.count`,
  `muzzle.life`, `sound.dur`, `sound.vol`) — the note names only the ones that row actually has;
* a `fireRate` above `BALANCE.weapons.rateMax` (15) is **clipped, not refused**, because
  `shotsPerSecond` takes the lesser of the two, so such a row measures the frame-budget ceiling and
  not the number typed.

### The bug it found on the way, in itself
`copyRow`/`restoreRow` treated every object the same, and `Object.assign({}, ['pierce','ricochet'])`
is `{0:'pierce', ...}`. `game/upgrades.js` `spendableBy` reads that list with `indexOf` at every
level-up, so a lance run died three minutes into a batch on `cannot.indexOf is not a function`. It
survived a whole afternoon of pulse probes because **only three of the five guns carry the list**
(arc, lance, swarm). `cloneValue` now copies arrays as arrays, and there is an end-to-end test that
plays a whole lance run, not just a unit test of the copy.

### What it measured, once, for real
The Swarm watch that session 96 left open ("if it becomes the obvious pick in the hangar, trim the
pair's damage"), six seeds at a ten minute window, six shards, **2m03s wall**:

| swarm shell damage | alive | median score | vs shipped | kills | bodies/s |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1.25 | 6/6 | 74,309 | 0.97x | 3,957 | 6.59 |
| **1.5 (shipped)** | 6/6 | 76,796 | 1.00x | 4,088 | 6.81 |
| 2 | 6/6 | 76,629 | 1.00x | 4,170 | 6.95 |

So the Swarm is sitting on a **plateau on its upper side**: a third more damage per shell buys
nothing measurable (score flat, level actually down 55→53), and the only lever in that range is the
down side, worth 3% for a 17% cut. If it ever has to be trimmed, that is the number to trim and
that is what it will cost. No change shipped — it is inside the band today.

The swept shipped value reading exactly `1.00x` in that table is the tool's cheapest self-check, and
it is in the test file too: a patch to the number already in the row must change nothing.

### One thing I decided not to pretend
`restoreRow` before every condition is **not load-bearing today**: each condition re-applies its own
whole patch, so with the current condition builder a missed restore changes nothing — a mutation
that deletes it keeps all 23 tests green, which I checked rather than assumed. It stays as a guard
for ordering (a condition builder that patches different fields per row would need it), and the test
that sits nearest to it says exactly that in its comment rather than claiming to prove it.

### Verified
Full suite **2375/2375** (23 new in `test/gun-tune.test.mjs`), `tools/simulate.js --seed 20261006`
unchanged, `node --check` clean on both new files. Mutation-checked three ways: copying arrays as
objects reddens 4 tests (including the end-to-end lance run), dropping the shipped control reddens 4,
deleting the per-condition restore reddens none (see above).

### What should come next
1. **The rest of the owed list**: the browser half of the performance pass (a THICK CROWD run
   standing 150 bodies on a scheduled run), silhouettes for the crowd pairs that share a colour, the
   afterimage's flat top of the ladder, and the deliberate FAIL on the difficulty band.
2. **`tools/line-ab.js` and `tools/gun-tune.js` now overlap on `--set`** but patch different tables
   (`BALANCE.upgrades.<line>` and `BALANCE.weapons.<gun>`). If a third tool ever wants the same
   knob, the patch/restore/label machinery should move into `tools/headless/` rather than be written
   a third time.
3. `domWrites()` per frame during a busy 150-body fight, so the performance pass has a number for
   "the page is quiet".

## Session 135 — the frame ruler counts the page. Not released (a tool and its tests)

### The number the performance pass was missing
Session 131 added `domWrites()` to the harness and said the next session should turn "the page is
quiet" into a number for the performance pass. It belongs in `tools/perf-probe.js`, which already
measures a scene two ways — the step in milliseconds and the painter in canvas operations — so it now
measures it a third: **writes to the DOM per painted frame**, on the same frames the painter is counted
on, because those are the frames the interface is painted on.

### What it says
Every gated scene writes the page **0.00 times a frame**, worst frame included:

| scene | bodies | ops mean | ops worst | page/frame | page worst |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| the schedule at full crowd | 100 | 1,970 | 2,014 | 0.00 | 0 |
| endless at the body wall | 200 | 2,951 | 3,012 | 0.00 | 0 |
| the same crowd, dying | 200 | 3,407 | 3,642 | 0.00 | 0 |
| the same crowd, spread out | 200 | 1,345 | 1,398 | 0.00 | 0 |
| PLAN section 2's sentence | 600 | 8,507 | 9,922 | 0.00 | 0 |

That is not the harness failing to see anything: the score, the purse and the level line are painted
**on the canvas** with the fight (`render/hud.js`), so a busy arena genuinely does not touch the page.
The DOM is only the screens around the arena.

### The budget, and why it is 1 and not 0
`PAGE_WRITES = 1` write a frame, gated on the mean, with the worst frame printed and not gated. Zero
would be the honest reading of today and a false alarm the day a card legitimately arrives in the
middle of a scene's window — that is a burst of a couple of dozen writes spread over ~180 frames, a
mean of a fraction. A panel *rebuilt* every frame (session 125's death-card bug) reads tens a frame.
The gap between the two is what the budget sits in.

A second test pins the strong claim directly — `a busy arena writes the page not at all` asserts the
dying crowd's mean and worst are both exactly 0 — and carries **its own control**: the same counter on
the same boot is asked to see the pause panel come up (58 writes), because a zero from an instrument
that is not plugged in looks identical to a zero that means something.

### Verified
Full suite **2376/2376**, `tools/simulate.js --seed 20261006` unchanged. Mutation-checked: deleting
`game.resetDomWrites()` from the paint loop (so the count accumulates instead of being per frame)
reddens four tests, including the two new ones.

### What should come next
1. The browser half of the performance pass is still the half this cannot reach: a THICK CROWD run
   standing 150 bodies on a scheduled run, read off the F3 plate on a real machine.
2. Silhouettes for the crowd pairs that share a colour; the afterimage's flat top of the ladder; the
   deliberate FAIL on the difficulty band.
3. `tools/line-ab.js` and `tools/gun-tune.js` now both carry a `--set` knob over different tables; if
   a third tool wants one, move the patch/restore/label machinery into `tools/headless/`.

## Session 136 — the shape table counts what the crowd is landing. The cliff has a mechanism. Not released

### What was added
`tools/run-shape.js` printed the state of a batch minute by minute (bodies, level, hull left, score).
It now prints a **rate**: `hulls lost` — the middle **run's own** hull losses since the previous row.
It rides on a new field in `stats()`, `hullLost: world.tally.hullLost`, which the tally already kept
(`game/tally.js noteHullLoss`) and no headless tool could read as a count.

The one design decision worth keeping: the column is **not** the difference of two slices' medians.
The fifth minute's median is over six survivors and the first's over forty-eight, so subtracting them
is a fact about which runs survived, not about whether anyone was being hit. Each run is read against
itself, and a run that was untouched says so.

### What it says — the owed difficulty band finally has a mechanism
48 seeds, the person bot, cards by die, the 15-minute cap, `--shards 8` (52 seconds of wall clock):

| at | flying | bodies | level | hull | hulls lost |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1m | 46 | 19 | 4 | 3 | 0 |
| 2m | 34 | 31 | 5.5 | 2 | 1 |
| 3m | 21 | 45 | 6 | 3 | 1 |
| 4m | 10 | 55.5 | 8 | 3 | 2 |
| 5m | 6 | 38.5 | 33.5 | 3 | 2.5 |
| 6m | 4 | 22.5 | 38.5 | 3 | 0.5 |
| 7m | 4 | 19 | 43.5 | 3 | 1.5 |
| 8m | 4 | 19 | 46.5 | 3 | 0 |
| 9m | 4 | 24 | 50 | 3 | 0.5 |
| 10m–14m | 4 | 12–21 | 54 → 63.5 | 3 | **0, 0, 0, 0, 0** |

Session 105 wrote "it is not a ramp, it is a cliff" from the death histogram and left it there. Now
the mechanism is on the page: **from the tenth minute the survivors are not touched at all**, at level
46–63, with 12–29 bodies on the screen. And the crowd is thinning, not because the director stopped
spawning — the wall is 100 — but because a strong ship **out-kills the spawn rate**: bodies fall from
55 at 4m to 12 at 14m. A crowd that cannot reach the ship cannot hurt it, and a ship that kills it
faster than it arrives makes that self-reinforcing.

`waves.maxBodies` is a ceiling. Nothing in the game puts a floor under what the crowd is *landing*.
That is the shape the mechanic PLAN's item already calls for ("punishes being cornered instead of
killing for it") has to be aimed at, and it is now a number rather than a guess. **No balance was
changed this session** — the fix is a feature, and it should be one deliberate session with the band
re-measured after it, not a dial nudged at 2 a.m.

A note on reading the `hull` column: it stays at 3 for the survivors even where hulls *are* being
lost, because the `hull` upgrade line (5 ranks, `step: 1`) puts hull back. That is exactly why the
rate column is needed — state does not answer "is anything landing".

### Verified
Full suite **2379/2379** (3 new tests in `test/run-shape.test.mjs`, two of them end-to-end through a
played batch), `tools/simulate.js --seed 20261006` unchanged. Mutation-checked: making a missing hull
tally print `0` instead of `-` reddens the test that holds that a dash is not a finding.

### What should come next
1. **The late-game floor**, now that it is measured. Not a dial: something that keeps the crowd
   arriving at a rate a level-60 ship cannot outrun, or that makes distance to the ship the thing that
   kills. Re-run `tools/run-shape.js --shards 8` (under a minute) and `tools/difficulty-arc.js` after
   it — the band is the check, and the hangar's prices are priced off these scores, so a change that

2. The browser half of the performance pass; silhouettes for the crowd pairs that share a colour; the

3. If a third tool wants a `--set` knob, move the patch/restore/label machinery out of `line-ab.js`

## Session 137 — one `--set` reader for three tools, and two more dials measured and refused. Not released

### What was built
`tools/headless/patch.js`: the shared `path=value` knob. `fieldAt` (dotted, goes through arrays —
`gap.0`), `numberFields`, `parseNumberPatch` (refuses a path that is not there and a path that is not
a number), `applyPatches` (a patch remembers the leaf it covered; restoring touches that leaf and
nothing else), `patchWords` (the header says what was moved).

It is now behind `tools/line-ab.js`, `tools/gun-tune.js` and — new — **`--set` on
`tools/difficulty-arc.js` and `tools/run-shape.js`**, which is the third tool my own notes said should
trigger the move rather than a third copy. `run-shape` passes `--set` through to its shards, and both
tools print it in their header so a patched batch can never be read back as the shipped game.

Two side effects worth having:
* **gun-tune no longer copies a row at all.** Session 134's array-became-an-object bug is not merely
  tested for now, it is unrepresentable: a patch touches one leaf. `copyRow`/`restoreRow` are gone.
* `run-shape` answers a bad flag with a line and exit 2 instead of a stack trace.

### What it measured, in about a minute a probe
The lever session 136 named was the **arrival rate**, not the crowd budget. Both halves of it, 48 seeds,
the person bot, the 15-minute cap, `--shards 8` (~50 s each):

| | middle death | died | in the band | the survivors at 14m |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| shipped | 2m36s | 44/48 | **6 (13%)** | level 63, 108k, hull 3, nothing landing |
| `waves.gap` 0.9–1.4 → 0.5–0.8 | **2m13s** | 45/48 | **3 (6%)** | level 87, 201k, hull 3, nothing landing |
| `waves.waveMaxPoints` 30 → 60 | 2m32s | 44/48 | **7 (15%)** | level 73, 140k, hull 3, nothing landing |

Nearly twice the arrivals **makes the band worse**: it kills the weak sooner and feeds the strong, whose
score doubles. Bigger waves nudge the band by two points and leave the cliff exactly where it was. The
`hulls lost` column reads 0 for the survivors in every one of the three batches.

So the ninth and tenth dials are spent, and the conclusion of session 105's ten survives: **no number
in `balance.js` reaches the band, because the band is not a rate problem.** A run that survives its
first four minutes out-kills the crowd's arrival rate at any arrival rate the table can express, and
the extra bodies are income. What is left is the thing PLAN's own item already named — a mechanic about
*where the ship is standing*, not about how many bodies arrive.

### Verified
Full suite **2392/2392** (9 new in `test/patch.test.mjs`, 2 in `test/difficulty-arc.test.mjs`, 2 in
`test/run-shape.test.mjs`), `tools/simulate.js --seed 20261006` unchanged. The new arc test proves the
patch reaches the game rather than only the header: the same four seeds, patched and unpatched, give
different death counts.

### What should come next
1. **The late-game mechanic**, and it has to be a mechanic. Everything a dial can do has now been
   measured eleven times. The shape it has to have is written in the numbers above: something that
   makes a ship that is not being touched *lose something* (its income, its range, its safety) rather
   than something that sends more bodies to be killed.
2. The browser half of the performance pass; silhouettes for the crowd pairs that share a colour; the
   afterimage's flat top of the ladder.

## Session 138 — the shard plumbing, written once instead of four times. Not released

### What was duplicated
`parseSeeds`, `splitShards`, `readRows`, `writeRows` and a ~28-line `playSharded` existed in
`tools/run-shape.js`, `tools/weapon-ladder.js` and `tools/gun-tune.js` — the last two importing the
first's seed helpers, which is the wrong direction anyway. They had already drifted: `gun-tune`'s
`readRows` was missing the "held no runs" check the other two had, so an empty `--in` there reported a
batch of none.

### What there is now
`tools/headless/shards.js`: `parseSeeds`, `splitShards`, `writeRows`, `readRows`, `playSharded`. The
module cannot know whose child it is starting, so a caller passes its own `import.meta.url` as `tool` —
a child that ran the module instead of the tool would play nothing at all. The rules are written down
in its header (round-robin dealing, a dead shard is an error naming its seeds, an empty pool is
refused, the tmp files are removed).

**And the arc tool can shard now**, which it could not before: `--seeds 1-96 --shards 8`, plus
`--out/--play-only` and `--in` for pooling. That is why this refactor was worth doing rather than
tidying: session 137's dial probes had to be run through `run-shape` because `difficulty-arc` could
not be parallelised, and a 48-seed arc is now a ~1-minute command instead of a ~25-minute one.

### Verified
- Full suite **2401/2401** (7 new in `test/shards.test.mjs`, 2 in `test/difficulty-arc.test.mjs`).
- The promise that makes sharding legal at all is a test now: **the same four seeds give a byte-identical
  report sharded and unsharded** (`a sharded batch is the same batch as one played in a single
  process`). Before this session that was an assumption.
- The shard module's own tests use a stand-in tool that writes what it is handed, so "a shard that dies
  is an error naming its seeds", "every seed played exactly once" and "no file left behind" are checked
  without playing a game.
- `tools/simulate.js --seed 20261006` unchanged; no game file touched.
- Both refactored sharding paths run for real: `weapon-ladder --shards 2` and `gun-tune --shards 2`.

The whole 48-seed arc, sharded: **48 seconds**, and it reproduces the shipped numbers exactly
(13% in the band FAIL, DRIFTER widest at 39% PASS) — the same report the ~25-minute unsharded run
gave in sessions 136 and 137.

### What should come next
1. **The late-game mechanic** — see session 136's mechanism and session 137's eleven refused dials. It
   has to make a ship that is not being touched *lose* something. Now that a 48-seed arc is a minute,
   the loop for trying one is short, which is the most it can be said to have got easier.
