## Session 147 — a ruler for the room a fight leaves, and the hive stops dying in its own split. Shipped 1.9.7

### What was on the shelf
Item 4 of 146's list, which is the same item 139, 143, 144, 145 and 146 left: *the late game wants a
fight and not a crowd*. It has stayed on the list because of the sentence 139 wrote beside it - every
instrument here measures the *dodging*, and the bot steps off every telegraph it is shown, so "a strong
run beats all three fights without losing a hull from the tenth minute on" could be repeated but not
argued with. A session cannot densify a fight it has no way of reading, so this session built the ruler
instead of the change: `tools/boss-pressure.js`.

### What the ruler is
It never asks whether a ship gets hit - that is the dodging, and it is measured. It asks how much of the
cage a ship may sit in and **stay** sitting in, which is a fact about the fight. The room is the live box
the arena shuts round the duel (`world.field`, which `fieldHalfWidth` has already held a hull and a
margin off the walls, so nothing is inset twice), cut into 10 px cells: one cell is one place a ship's
centre can be, and a hull-width apart is as near as two places can be. A place **stands** if nothing
claims it, and every claim is made with the test the hit itself would use, clipped to the horizon:

```
  a shell in the air      `capsule`, `shot.r + ship.r`, walked forward across the horizon
  a lock it is holding    `axisDistance`, to the same wall the beam is clipped at
  a shell it is arming    as far as that wall could have travelled, minus the door it is holding open
  a fan it is showing     the whole arc the blades will travel, `offTheBlade` with a near end
  a blade already loose   the arc still in front of it, and not the one behind
  a body standing there   the fight, its mass, its brood, its calls: `enemy.r + ship.r`
  a call it is making     the marks on the rim, at the size of the body that will arrive on one
```

One rule makes the whole thing a measurement and not a fear-map: **a telegraph claims a place only when
there is not a whole promise left to leave it in** - `beatTimeLeft(boss) <= horizon`. A spoke with 0.6 s
to go is a place you may stand; the same spoke with 0.2 s left is a wall. The default horizon *is*
`bosses.telegraphMin`, PLAN 3.4's own promise, so the headline column means "the room left to a ship
that has one promise to answer" and not a duration invented here. A **fired** beam claims nothing at all,
because `spendBeam` pays out on the step it is fired and the light left behind is the record of it.

To read a promise at all the tool needed three numbers the frame never asks for, and they are read
helpers in `game/bosses.js` now, beside the four the renderer already borrows: `beatTimeLeft` (a
duration, not `beatProgress`'s share - a third of a 0.7 s wind-up and a third of a 1.05 s one are not
the same amount of time to be out of), `shellShot` (the row `throwRing` will fill its shot from, so a
wall can be counted where it will have got to), and `armRate` (which way a lit fan turns).

### The bug the ruler walked into
Holding the hive at its third phase, the run threw: `killEnemy` on a body that was already buried. The
phase-3 split sheds the honeycomb through `breakMass` -> `killEnemy`, and a cell's `onDeath` is
`cellComesOff`, which charges the bar for the mass coming off - on top of `spendSplit`, which is the
framework paying that same `count x share` (30% of the hive's whole length) once and honestly. A hive
that reached its last phase with the mass whole and then took one fat hit across the last mark had less
on the bar than the shed was worth, the bar went to zero *inside* the shed, and the split buried a boss
that was already buried. `shedCore` now lets go of `cell.hub` before it kills the cell, which is exactly
what `cellComesOff`'s existing `hub === null` guard was written for: a shed the run did not shoot is not
the run's to pay for. Reachable in an ordinary late run - a late blast is a few percent of the hive's
bar, and the window is only 3% wide because that is how deep the third mark sits. The sim's reference
run never walked into it, which is why it survived; the sim does not pin a boss's hull and look.

### What it says
40 s of each phase of each fight, 400 readings a phase, the fight held at the middle of its own band and
the ship parked in the cage's middle and invulnerable:

```
                      standable   worst   in a corner   biggest piece   spots
  Warden   phase 3      95.4%     87.1%       0.0%          87.7%         1.9
  Hive     phase 3      96.6%     95.4%       0.0%          96.6%         1.0
  sun      phase 3      92.1%     75.0%       0.0%          91.9%         1.3
```

At the game's own promise the fights barely contest space: **no reading of no phase of no fight has ever
put the ship in a corner** (under 40% free). Ask the same room three seconds ahead and it does bite - the
Warden falls to 86.8%, the sun to 81.0% with a worst moment of 52.5% free split into 2.3 pieces of glass
- which says the wall is there and arrives only for a ship that is not watching. The Hive does not move
at all between 0.6 s and 3 s, and that is the ruler's own limit and not the hive's: a shell, a spoke, a
fan and a blade all travel a line the fight has already shown, but a brood *steers*, so a body can only
be claimed where it is standing. Its column is the one to disbelieve first, and the parked ship is
standing in the least free span of glass in that room. Also flattering by construction: no crowd (the
director holds during a duel), nothing shoots back so every ring is aimed at a ship that never moved,
and the mass is whole because nothing is shooting cells off.

### One draft that was wrong and how it was caught
The first `sweep` walked a blade's arc in sub-angles and claimed a band at each. Two sub-angles `d` apart
leave a hole `reach x d - 2 x half` wide at the far end of a long blade - a hole in a claim is a place
the tool swears is safe - and `test/boss-pressure.test.mjs`'s loose-blade test found it by asking about
a place in the middle of the arc. A sweep is claimed as an arc now: `offTheBlade` asked at whichever
bearing of the sweep lies nearest the place, once per place instead of once per step - exact, and the
whole nine-row look still runs in about a second.

### Verified
Full suite **2471/2471** (2458 at HEAD, +12 in `test/boss-pressure.test.mjs` and +1 in
`test/hive.test.mjs`). `tools/simulate.js --seed 20261006 --trace` byte for byte what it was - 10m00s /
73,982 / level 57 - checked against a trace generated from a clean worktree of HEAD in the same session,
twice: once after the hive fix and once after the read helpers, because a ruler is not a game and had
better not move one. The new test file was mutation-checked claim by claim - the promise gate left wide
open (2 tests red), a shell that forgets its door (1), a shell that claims only where it stands (1), a
body that claims its own radius and not its reach (1), a shown fan ignored (1), loose blades ignored (2),
a sweep that claims only where the blade is standing (1), the room inset a second time (1). One mutation
survives and is named for what it is: reading the *direction* a blade sweeps (`armRate`'s sign) cannot be
caught, because no row in the shipped table turns a blade backwards. `node --check` on every file
touched, every added line ASCII and under 102 columns, and the whole nine-row look runs in 1.2 s.

### What should come next
1. **The densification, which has a PLAN item now and a ruler to price it with.** Two asks, in the order
   that does least damage to what is already good: one more thing to be out of at the same time in each
   fight's last phase, or read `tierBonus.telegraph` into the bosses' own wind-ups (they do not read it
   at all today, and 139 measured that a 20% shorter tell moves a late death count by 0.6 - on the
   crowd, which was the half that could be measured). Either way the first two phases stay wide: they are
   tutorials, and the table above says they currently are, which is a fact worth keeping.
2. **The Hive column is a known blind spot in the ruler.** If a session wants to believe it, the way to
   do that is to claim a brood's place *and* the place it is steering to - `swarmlings.js` knows the turn
   rate and the target, so a projected body is a few lines and one more test - and say which of the two
   readings the table is using.
3. **The shape audit's list is still not gated** (carried from 145 and 146): nothing pins that
   `tools/shape-lab.js`'s three lists hold the pairs `test/palette-read.test.mjs` names, so a change to
   colour spacing quietly rewrites what the audit claims to have checked.
4. Unchanged from 139-146: the XP curve is a decision to take on purpose with the hangar re-priced after
   it; the browser half of the performance pass is the owner's; and `tools/power-ladder.js` has not been
   re-read since the deck grew the afterimage.

## Session 148 — a beat can carry one: the Warden's last phase now walls the room twice at once. Shipped 1.9.8

### What was on the shelf
The same item again - 139, 143, 144, 145, 146, 147 left it, and 147 finally built the ruler
(`tools/boss-pressure.js`) so that it could be argued with instead of repeated. The reading 147 took
was: at the game's own promise (`bosses.telegraphMin`, 0.6 s) the last phase leaves 95.4% of the cage
standable under the Warden, 96.6% under the Hive, 92.1% under the sun, and *no* phase of *any* fight
ever had the ship cornered; three seconds out the Warden falls to 86.8% and the sun to 81.0%, and the
Hive does not move at all. PLAN's own note beside the item named the lever as "how many things a beat
gives you to be out of at once", and suggested a ring that comes with a spoke lock.

### The mechanism: a beat that carries one (`with`, in `game/bosses.js`)
The first thing I tried was the number, and it was wrong in a way worth writing down. Slapping
`with: 'spokes'` on phase 3's `bullets` row did make the halt carry both - but the framework then
*also* took `spokes` on its own turn through the rotation, so the phase threw four spokes every ride
**and** eight more out of the ring stop: the fan doubled and the fight went silly. A carried beat is
therefore not available to the rotation: `foldsRow` asks "does any row of this phase carry you?" and
`takeBeat` refuses one that does, and `carriedBeatsOf` (exported) walks a phase's whole `with` table -
it is what both the tool and the tests read the pairing off.

So a pair is: `takeBeat` draws the carrier, and the carried one is hung on the same halt as `pair`
(`showBeat` for both, one `takeTheBeat` with the longer of the two wind-ups as the clock - the promise
has to cover both asks, and the shorter one just holds its telegraph longer); `landBeat` fires both
halves and clears `pair` in one place, so nothing can land half a stop; and `putThePlaceDown` and
`putThePromiseDown` clear the pair with the halt, so a phase change or a flare mid-stop puts *both*
halves down and nothing is left standing in the arena with no telegraph behind it. `windupProgress`
reads the pair's wind-up when there is one, so the arc the renderer draws and the wall the tool counts
are the same promise. Validation is out loud: a `with` that names a row the phase never wrote, a beat
carrying itself, and a carried beat carrying one of its own all throw - the quiet version is a boss
that stops doing one of its attacks and nobody noticing which one. One wart from the row shape: the
Warden's `spokes` is a bare count with its wind-up and beam beside it, so a lock is something a beat
can carry and never one that carries (`isRow`), which is written in `carriedBeat`'s comment before
somebody hunts it.

**Why a pair instead of "both at once"**: the second promise is bought out of the *ride*, so the player
gets more to be out of per halt without getting less time per halt. A denser beat, not a louder fight
- and `sent/s` in the ruler is the column that keeps that honest.

### `sent/s`, and the price of it
The tool now counts things *sent into the room* per second - shots, beams/blades, called bodies, off
the fight's own counters (`bossShots`, `bossBeams`, `bossBlades`, `bossSummons` are exported for it,
and `thingsSent(boss)` is the sum). The Warden's last phase went 6.15 -> 11.05 things a second, which
is the whole argument for pricing a pair. A ride long enough to pay that off in full is about 4.2 s
(`sent/s` back to 6.80), and asking the ruler about *that* one is the finding: 95.7% standable and
87.8% biggest piece at the promise, 87.4% with a worst moment of 55.9% three seconds out - which is
where the phase stood unpaired. A ride that pays for a pairing in full buys the nothing that paying it
off in full means, so the phase pays what it can: `wait` 1.8 -> 2.4 s, and the reading is 95.4 -> **93.4%** standable at the promise, biggest free piece 87.7 -> **80.8%**, free
pieces in view 1.9 -> **2.4**; three seconds out, 86.8 -> **79.6%**, worst moment 59.8 -> **51.7%**,
biggest piece 71.2 -> **63.6%**, pieces 2.8 -> **4.6**. It is the first phase in the game that both
wants the ship in a place and walls that place off.

The volley's own `shake` went 10 -> 6. Not for the reason I first wrote: the shake on that step is the
volley's plus the ring's 8 plus **one per beam fired** (`fireBeam` shakes per beam, so eight spokes are
8 px of it), which at 10 hit the 18 px cap and had some clipped away; at 6 the same stop peaks at 17.7.

### Why the other two fights did not get one
- **The Eclipse tried it and it went back.** `sweep` carrying `bullets` moved the phase from 92.1% to
  90.9% at the promise, which is nothing - and the reason is geometric and is now written on the phase:
  the door is `2 x gap` = **1.0 rad** wide and a blade's band is `arc` = **0.9 rad**, so a door that
  opens centred on a band has 0.1 rad of standable wedge left, some 40 px of arc at the far edge of the
  sun's band. The fan and the wall are each about as wide as the other's only answer. Pairing them is
  not a harder question, it is a question with no room in the answer. What the sun needs is a beat that
  walls nothing - bodies on marks, which it has never had.
- **The Hive does not move the ruler at all** (96.6% before and after, at every horizon), because its
  whole attack is bodies that steer and a steering body cannot be projected. Its pressure is a timing
  problem for a ship that is moving, not a map of places not to be. Left completely alone.

### What the change made untrue elsewhere
`test/warden.test.mjs`'s table test asserted every phase's `wait` was shorter than the last one. That
rule was written when patience *was* the escalation; a phase that buys a second promise with a longer
ride is not breaking it, it is paying for it. The rule is now conditional - a longer ride has to come
with a halt that carries - and the honest version is measured: **each phase of the ring sends more than
the one before it, measured** holds each phase in its own band of the bar for half a minute and compares
`thingsSent` per second (1.20 / 4.90 / 11.05). `test/bosses.test.mjs` got the pairing walk (every `with`
in the shipped tables names a row its own phase wrote, and the shipped pair is written down so an
unpairing has to say so) and the miswrite refusals. New warden tests: both halves on one halt, landing
on one step, no plain spoke halt left in the phase that carries, phase 2 still alternating (the pair is
a phase and not a rule), a flare putting both halves down, and - the fairness guard for a pair - that
some bearing inside the door it opens is off every spoke line by more than a spoke is wide, so a pair
can never open a door that is all spoke. Both new mechanisms were mutation-checked: take the `with` out
and six tests fail; make `takeBeat` ignore the carry and seven fail. Suite 2472 -> **2481**.

### The run, and one thing that is not in the tree
Reference run (seed 20261006, aware bot, 10 min cap): `score 73354 level 57`, was 73982 - 0.8%, same
trace shape, `hull 3` at the end with the Warden down at 19800 as ever. The bot cannot see any of this:
it steps off telegraphs, so a denser halt costs it nothing, and a human-facing fight change is not
visible in a run. That is what the ruler is for and it is now said in the entry below rather than
learned twice. A `--at 295 --bot human` batch did shuffle a couple of deaths between the crowd and the
fight on 6 seeds, which is noise at that sample size and I left it there.

**Finding**: PLAN line ~150 and several NOTES entries point at `release-checks/difficulty-baseline.md`
and at `docs/` (feel.mjs, first-run.md, world-map.mdx) and at `tools/difficulty-baseline.js`. **None of
those paths exist in this working copy** and `git log --all` has no history for them. The reference
numbers are therefore recorded only in NOTES and CHANGELOG. I did not re-create the folders; whoever
wants that record written from a tool again has to decide what belongs in it. I also removed a
verbatim duplicate of this PLAN item that was sitting as the last line of PLAN.md (session 147 wrote
the annotated one 25 lines above it and a bare copy got appended).

### Next
1. The sun wants the beat that walls nothing: `call` on the Eclipse's last phase - marks on the rim,
   bodies to clear, and the ruler should finally move for that fight. Price it against the fan, not
   against the shell.
2. The Hive's last phase is unreadable by this ruler. Either give it one telegraphed non-body beat so
   the instrument can see it, or write the read for steering bodies (walk a brood's steering over the
   horizon, which is a real tool and not a small one).
3. Still open from earlier sessions: the **shot-speed line** (four seeds cannot tell 0.98 from 1.02;
   needs ~20 seeds); whether the **first two minutes** are too harsh for a new player (needs a human);
   and reading the tier's `tierBonus.telegraph` into the bosses' own wind-ups, which is the other ask
   PLAN names and is one line in `bosses.js` - it would change the feel of every fight in a deep run,
   so it wants its own session and its own ruler reading.

## Session 149 — the sun's last phase grows a third beat: bodies on marks, carried by the wall. Shipped 1.9.9

### What was on the shelf
The same PLAN item, for the fourth session running. Session 148 ended it with "what is left of this
item is those two fights, and the lever for them is a beat that walls nothing - bodies on marks,
which the sun has never had", so this session did the sun. The Hive is left, and the note at the end
has the move for it.

### The beat (`call` on `eclipse` phase 3, `game/balance.js`)
Three of the crowd's own darters, on three marks lit 0.8 rad apart, 40 px outside the sun's rim, on
the bearing the ship is *not* standing on, held 0.95 s and then walked out of. Nothing in
`game/bosses.js` had to be built for it: the ring's summons (`windCall`, `sendCall`, `marksAt`)
already knew how to light a fan of places and fill them, and a sun is a body with a rim like a ring
is. What the row had to answer was where to hang it and what it costs.

**It is carried by the shell, not by the fan** (`with: 'call'` on the `bullets` row). Session 148 had
already worked out and written down why the fan and the wall cannot be paired here - a 1.0 rad door
inside a 0.9 rad blade band is 0.1 rad of answer - and had left the sentence "bodies on marks, say,
which is the one beat the sun has never had" pointing at this row. So the fan keeps its turns alone,
the shell carries the call, and the halt is held for the longer of the two wind-ups, which means the
door is now shown for 0.95 s instead of 0.72: the one kindness in the phase, and it is in the same
stop as the threat. The ride went 1.85 -> 2.0 s to pay for the second promise, the way session 148
paid for the Warden's pair, and the whole argument is the same one: a denser beat, not a louder fight.

**Why 40 px and not the ring's 26.** The marks stand 98 px out from the middle of a sun whose drag
lets go of the ship at 92 (`pull.floor`). A mark inside that floor is a place a ship being dragged
sunwards drifts into by itself, and a place you arrive at by falling is not a place you were shown and
then charged for. Outside the floor, standing off a mark is a thing the engines do. That is the whole
number, and it is why a call's `gap` is priced per phase and not per framework.

**The marks are punched out of the night** (`render/darkness.js` `punchCall`, new number
`dark.light.mark` = 34 px). This is the only phase in the game that is both dark (0.86) and summons,
and a mark the veil has eaten is no promise - `telegraphMin` does not care how dark the room is. Full
weight like a shot and not part weight like the door, because a mark is where a body is about to
arrive and not a place to be standing. The bodies that come out of them need no light of their own:
they walk, into the ship's own 300 px.

### The framework change, which was the real work
A `call` used to *jump the queue*: `alternateBeats` opened with "if this phase calls and nothing of
the last call is standing, call", and took its ordinary turn otherwise. That rule is a summoner. Over
a minute of the Warden's last phase with every pack killed the step it lands - which is what a strong
run does - the fight spent **all seventeen of its stops on calls and never lit its door once**. It is
in `test/warden.test.mjs` now, and the order string it fails with is the whole bug: `CCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCC`.

So `call` is a turn of the rotation like any other row (`BEAT_ROWS_ROTATION`), and a turn it cannot
take goes to the beat behind it rather than being taken anyway. `takeBeat` keeps one rule of its own
for a carried call: a pair whose call finds the room occupied asks the one question it was always
asking, because a pairing must not be an exception to the rule it is paired with. `leadBeat` gained
the call behind the fan and ahead of the shell, which is where a phase whose only news is a call opens
(the Warden's third phase did that before this change too, by the old preemption, and
`test/warden.test.mjs` noticed the first time I left it out - that test is the reason the line is
there and it says so).

### Readings (`tools/boss-pressure.js`, Eclipse phase 3, at the game's own 0.6 s promise)
Against a worktree of HEAD, same seed, same watch:

| | standable | worst moment | biggest piece | sent/s | bodies claim |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| before | 92.1% | 75.0% free | 91.9% | 5.85 | 0.8% |
| after | 91.4% | 70.3% free | 90.9% | 6.60 | 1.0% |

The tight place got four and a half points tighter and the room barely moved: which is what a beat
that walls nothing is *for*, and the marks themselves claim 0.0% because a place punched full weight
out of the night is a place the fight has let go of and not a place that hurts. **The Warden's and the
Hive's nine numbers are byte for byte what they were**, which is the check that a rotation change in a
shared framework did not quietly reprice the two fights that were not supposed to change. Reference
run (seed 20261006, aware bot, 10 min): `score 73354 level 57`, identical to session 148 - the bot
never reaches the sun's last phase inside the window, so a fight change down there cannot show up in
it. That is what the ruler is for and it is said here rather than learned twice.

### Three things that cost me time and are worth writing down
1. **`killEnemy` does not write the hull.** `game/bosses.js` `living()` gates a call on "a body leaves
   the crowd by dying, so `hp` is the whole of the question", and `killEnemy` only takes the body out
   of the array - it is `damageEnemy` that writes `hp`. A test or tool that clears a room with
   `killEnemy` leaves the fight holding a pack that is not in the room, and the gate never opens
   again. My darkness test sat for 3000 frames waiting for a second call that its own cheating had
   forbidden. Either write `hp = 0` first (`tools/boss-pressure.js` does) or hurt it properly.
2. **A ruler must not answer what it measures.** My first version of this session made
   `tools/boss-pressure.js` kill every called body the step it landed, so that repeated calls could
   be seen. It worked, and it moved the shipped Warden's recorded phase-3 reading from 93.4%
   standable to 96.3% - a ship parked in a fight does not shoot, and the pack it is being shown is
   part of the room's claim. Reverted: the tool measures a ship that never shoots, its caveats say so,
   and the cadence of calls is measured in tests instead where the room *is* answered. Old numbers in
   NOTES stay comparable, which is the whole reason a ruler exists.
3. **A knife-edge test is an rng test.** `test/arms.test.mjs` pins that a blade hurts at exactly the
   width it is drawn at, and it started failing by 7e-14 once this row existed. Nothing about blades
   changed: a phase that takes a different sequence of beats asks the world's rng a different
   sequence of questions, so the arm's angle lands somewhere else and the float error on
   `half + sin(x)*half` came out on the other side of equality. The assertions now carry a named
   `hair = 1e-9` with the reason beside it, because a test that fails on fourteen powers of nothing
   gets deleted by the next session instead of read.

### Next
1. **The Hive's last phase, same lever.** The framework now lets any fight write a `call` as a turn of
   its rotation, and the Hive is the fight the ruler reads flattest because its whole attack is bodies
   that steer. A call there should be *bodies that come out of somewhere the ship chose not to be* -
   marks behind the rocks, say, or on the far side of the split - and the interesting question is
   whether a brood can be made to arrive in a way the instrument can see at all. Read session 148's
   caveat on steering bodies first.
2. Still open from earlier sessions: the **shot-speed line** (four seeds cannot tell 0.98 from 1.02;
   needs ~20 seeds); whether the **first two minutes** are too harsh for a new player (needs a human);
   and reading the tier's `tierBonus.telegraph` into the bosses' own wind-ups - one line in
   `bosses.js`, and it would change the feel of every fight in a deep run, so it wants its own session
   and its own ruler reading.

## Session 150 — the ruler could not see a brood; read, the second boss was never the flattest fight in the game

### What was on the shelf
Session 149's first next-item: give the Hive's last phase the same lever the Warden and the sun just
got. It came with a warning attached, and the warning is what this session actually worked on. Session
147 had written the caveat into the tool's own footnotes and into session 148's notes, and everyone
since had treated it as the reason the Hive's row could not be trusted: *a shell, a spoke, a fan and a
blade all travel a line the fight has already shown, so each of them can be counted where it will have
got to across the horizon. A brood steers, and nothing here can say where it will be in half a second,
so a body claims only the place it is standing.* Read that way the Hive is made of bodies and is the
flattest read of the three by construction - 96.6% standable in its third phase at the game's own
promise, against the sun's 92.1%. Which is why nobody had dared densify it: the ruler would have said
it was gentle, and then would have said it was gentle again.

The caveat is half wrong, and the half that is wrong is the half that mattered. A steering body cannot
be projected. A flock does not steer, though - it is a clock with three beats, and two of the three
say what is coming and exactly when:

- a pack already `DIVING` is flying a line its own `commit()` locked: direction fixed, pace fixed at
  `dive.mul` times the body's speed, time left on its timer;
- a pack `BRACED` has committed to a dive and not yet to a bearing - the bearing is taken from the
  ship at the moment it goes, and `game/flock.js` is not allowed to know where the ship will be. But
  it knows the *time*, and a threat whose time you know walls off a room whether or not you know
  which way it will point.

So: the line for the one, an aim-free room for the other.

### The two reads (`game/flock.js` `divePace`, `nextDive`)
`divePace` is the speed `game/kinds.js` `committed` actually glides a pack at - `speed * (1 - frost) *
dive.mul`, with the frost off it because a dive is a walk like every other - and nought for a body
with no pack, which has no line and nothing to fly it at. `nextDive` answers all three beats, because
a pack's beat is a clock and not a coin toss: a `DIVING` body has no wait and as much of the dive as
its timer has left; a `BRACED` one has the whole of `dive.time` in front of it and the bunching to
get through first; a gathering one has that same dive plus the rest of the gathering, and has promised
nothing about *where*, which is why the read of it is a room and not a lane and why the approach is
never counted. Both are exported for the tool and nothing else, on the `packOf`/`isDiving` precedent
from session 147: the tool borrows the game's numbers rather than carrying its own.

### The claims (`tools/boss-pressure.js`)
Two new claim columns, `arrive` and `dive`, and one new column that is not a claim:

- `claimDives` lays a **capsule** along a locked line: from where the body stands to `pace * min(left,
  horizon - wait)` further along, fattened by `body.r + player.r` - a lane, not a disc, and the lane
  ends where the dive ends. `reaches()` was already general enough to take any centre and any length;
  it only ever had the fight's shells to work with before.
- `claimBrood` files everything else in the brood as a **disc of what it can reach** round where it
  stands, for the same reason the fight's own cells are read that way: it is true without knowing
  anything the instrument cannot know. `sight.js` `reaches` (an aim-free threat) was the shape;
  `claimCells` was the pattern; neither was changed.
- A dive a whole promise off is a threat and not a wall, so nothing beyond the body is claimed until
  `wait <= horizon`. That gate is the rule said in words: the arithmetic two lines down refuses it too
  (`horizon - wait` has gone negative), so it is not a branch a test can catch on its own, and the
  comment says so rather than pretending otherwise.
- `crowd` is how many bodies were standing in the room to be read. This is the number that tells you
  how much to believe the row, and it exists because nothing in here shoots back: a brood a fight
  calls is never called off, so over a long watch of a breeding fight the crowd only grows - the same
  phase reads 41 bodies at eight seconds and 216 at eighty, and the `arrive` share grows with it. That
  is not a bug in the read, it is the read telling you the state is not one a run is in. Rows were not
  re-cut to a shorter default watch: 40 s stays the house number so the twenty-one numbers already
  written down stay comparable, and `--seconds 8` is printed next to them in the footnotes.

### The bug the visit found, which was in the tool and not in the game
`Room.claimed` was a `Uint8Array` and `BIT.dive` is 256. The first run of the new tool said `dive 0.0`
for every phase of every fight while `arrive` moved by twenty points, which is the kind of number that
only happens: the geometry was right, the walk was right, and the grid had no bit to file the claim in,
so `paint()` stored 0 and `measure()` counted it under nothing. Widened to `Uint16Array` - bit 256 is
now a byte boundary away from being swallowed again - and `test/boss-pressure.test.mjs` has a test that
paints one cell per claim bit and refuses a claim that comes back as nothing or as something else, plus
the assertions that the bits are single, distinct and inside the width of the grid. Before this, adding
a claim to the ruler could silently do nothing at all, and did.

### The numbers, and the decision that falls out of them
Reference run (`--seed 7`) is **byte for byte what it was**, trace hash and all: both helpers are reads
and the tool does not run in a game. Suite at HEAD measured 2490 in the same minute, now 2496 (+4 in
`test/boss-pressure.test.mjs`, +2 in `test/swarm.test.mjs`). Hive at the game's own promise (40 s), and
then the fair 8 s watch beside the other two fights:

| phase | standable before | after | worst before | after | crowd at 8 s |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Hive 1 | 98.5% | 92.9% | 98.1% | 63.8% | 12 |
| Hive 2 | 97.6% | 84.3% | 97.0% | 62.3% | 23 |
| Hive 3 | 96.6% | 78.1% | 95.4% | 55.2% | 41 |

At 8 s: Hive 3 reads 90.8% standable / 58.3% worst, against the Warden's 93.7 / 87.6 and the sun's
91.3 / 69.6. Stable across seeds 3, 12 and 77 (88.2-88.5% and 58.6-62.4%). The Warden's and the sun's
nine numbers did not move a digit, because neither fight makes a body that steers.

**So the Hive gets no new beat.** It was already contesting more room at the promise than the two fights
that were densified on purpose, and its worst moment is tighter than either by a distance - the second
boss is the tightest of the three, not the flattest, and the PLAN item is ticked on that measurement
instead of on a fourth mechanism. The shape of it is worth writing down before anyone redesigns it: the
brood's pressure is **wave after wave and never one wall**. `standable` swings from 97% free to 63% free
between one sample and the next, and a probe over three minutes of phase 3 (`.scratch`, not shipped) says
why. The crowd commits every **4.57 to 4.61 s**, which is the flock's own cycle (`gather 3.4 + brace 0.7
+ dive 0.5`) and nothing else: a cohort keeps the clock it was born with, so whatever the fight is doing
the waves keep their own time and nothing is actually locked to the beat that threw it out. And the crowd
never goes at once: the biggest brood the probe saw was 234 bodies and the biggest whole-crowd commit was
66; the share of the brood diving at a commit settles round a half early and then falls away (`6/6,
12/18, 30/54, 72/144`). So the room is swept rather than shut, and a ship that keeps moving is inside the
waves rather than under one - which is the read's own account of why the average is comfortable and the
worst moment is not. Two wrong turns are worth naming so nobody repeats them: the whole crowd does not
commit in step (an earlier hour of this session believed it did, from one sample of 60 of 60, which was
one small cohort at the start of a watch), and the brood is not born on the fight's rotation - a
fragment's mouths light on the spawn row's own `gap` and `step`, so there is no single "the fleet beat is
4.55 s" to compare the waves against in the first place.

### Surprises
1. Four sessions of "the Hive is flat and here is why the ruler cannot say otherwise" and the reason was
   two missing lines. Worth keeping: a caveat that has been repeated three times stops being checked.
2. The silent bit width. Any claim added to this ruler before today could have vanished the same way and
   nobody would have seen a red test, because the tool's own test file had no reason to ask about a bit
   it had never used. The fix is not the widening, it is the test that paints every bit.
3. `crowd` is the column I did not ask for and would now not give up. A measurement that quietly counts a
   different situation than the one it names is worse than no measurement, and this one had been doing it
   since session 147: the crowd in a boss cage is not static, it is bred.
4. One mutation survived, and it is the one I expected: dropping `dive.wait > horizon` from `claimBrood`.
   It is arithmetically swallowed by the `away <= 0` guard below it, so no test can see it; the comment
   now says the gate is the rule in words and not a branch. Everything else died: the `Uint8Array` grid
   (2 tests red), `claimBrood` unwired (2 red), the arrival room widened to the whole dive at full pace
   (1 red), a `flock.js` `dive.mul` dropped (1 red), the gathering beat answering without the bunching in
   front of it (1 red), a braced pack reporting its dive as already flown (2 red).

### Left in the tree
`tools/boss-pressure.js` (two claim walks, `crowd`, two columns, rewrote two footnotes and the foreword),
`src/game/flock.js` (`divePace`, `nextDive`, exported for the tool), `test/boss-pressure.test.mjs` (+4),
`test/swarm.test.mjs` (+2), `PLAN.md` (the item ticked, with the reading and the correction written into
it). `tools/shape-lab.js`'s three lists, from session 147's third item, turned out to already be pinned: the
shape-lab ruler prints no lists at all, and the three that `tools/try-body.js` prints are one hand-named
pair list per heading with the ruler measuring every name in it - `sights.crowdedColours()` is the whole
third list, and `palette-read.test.mjs` asserts that every name in the other two earns its place as
measured. So there is no second copy of anything left to drift, which is what that item was after. No release: nothing a player sees or feels changed, and the reference run says so.

### Next
1. **The brood commits in waves, on a clock that is not the fight's.** A probe over three minutes of the
   Hive's last phase found a commit every 4.57-4.61 s no matter what the boss was doing, and never more
   than about half the crowd at once. Two questions live there and neither is answered yet. The legibility
   one: each body's own telegraph circle (`render/draw.js`, `braceProgress`) is the only tell, and a wave
   of 40 bodies arriving out of a 200-body crowd may need something coarser than a circle - but read the
   `BRACED` handling there first, because it may already be loud enough and the real question is whether
   it is legible at that many bodies. The design one: a fight whose brood keeps its own time is a fight
   with two clocks in it, and nobody wrote down whether that is the intention. `tools/boss-pressure.js`
   can price either answer, because the swing between 97% free and 63% free is what any such tell is
   selling.
2. **A tuning idea the ruler just made visible**: `bosses.telegraphMin` is 0.6 s and the flock's cycle is
   4.6 s, so the brood reads as a wave that arrives and goes. Raising the promise to 1 s would flatten
   the wave into a wall (the `arrive` share goes up and the peaks come down) and lowering it to 0.4 would
   make the brood feel like nothing until it is on you. Neither is obviously right. Do not change the
   promise on this note alone - it is the number the whole report is written against.
   The flattery this ruler still swallows is in the same direction, and it is the approach: a body can be
   read 400 px away while it walks toward you and is only credited with the place it stands. Anyone who
   wants to do something about that has to say how a steering body's approach may be forecast at all,
   which is the sentence session 147 left and which is still true for the third of a flock that has
   promised nothing. The tool's last footnote says all of this too.
3. Still open from earlier sessions: the **shot-speed line** (four seeds cannot tell 0.98 from 1.02;
   needs ~20 seeds) and whether the **first two minutes** are too harsh for a new player (needs a human).
   The third item on that list - reading the tier's `tierBonus.telegraph` into the bosses' own wind-ups -
   cannot be done as written: `tierBonus` exists nowhere in this working copy, in `src/` or in `tools/`,
   and PLAN has named it as though it were a live number since. Same class of stale plan-reference as
   session 148's missing `release-checks/` and `docs/game-balance.md`. Somebody has to decide whether the
   tier ladder of telegraphs is a thing this game should have, in which case it is designed from scratch,
   or a sentence to delete from PLAN.

## Session 151 — a clump of the swarm gets one tell: a ring that burns down over the brace, and a line for what is left of the dive

### What was on the shelf
Session 150's first next-item: the brood commits in waves and the only tell is each body's own nose
light, so "a wave of 40 bodies arriving out of a 200-body crowd may need something coarser than a
circle - but read the `BRACED` handling first, because it may already be loud enough". I read it, and
I measured before drawing anything, because "coarser" is a size and not an idea.

The census (`.scratch/brood-census.mjs`, a parked ship and the director left running from the swarm's
`from`): **three packs of 14-17 bodies on the arena at a time** in a late run's waves, rms spread
27-54 px while bracing (p50 40), 684 px/s of dive pace at that age, so 170-340 px of line, and at most
two clumps bracing or diving in any one sample. So the clump has a size, a handful of them are on the
glass, and per-body lights are the wrong grain for it. That is the whole argument for the shape, and
it is why the sizes in `render/flock.js` are what they are.

### What landed
**`src/render/flock.js`**, one entry point (`drawFlockTells(ctx, world.flocks)`), called from
`renderer.js` beside `drawTelegraphs` so both go under the bodies they describe. Two tells, one per
pack:

- **the brace is a clock** - a ring at the pack's middle, 10 px outside its own spread, in the game's
  warning hues: a faint whole circle (what the beat was), an arc of it left that gets eaten as the
  beat runs out, and one light at the head of that arc so the countdown has an end the eye can find.
  A part-of-a-circle closing over a circle is the grammar the ship's own dash ring and an elite's hull
  ring already use for a wait; the difference is direction, and it is on purpose - the dash ring
  *fills*, this one *burns down*. Brightness runs 0.18 -> 0.85 over the brace, so the last quarter is
  the loudest thing on the clump.
- **the dive is a line** - a soft trail (one baked `makeStreak`, stamped stretched, never rebuilt)
  from the middle out to `pace * time left` along the line the pack locked, with a light at the far
  end: *this* is how far the lunge gets. It shortens as the dive spends itself and stops at nothing,
  so no light outlives the promise it was drawn from. The geometry is deliberately the same capsule
  `tools/boss-pressure.js` `claimDives` lays - the game now draws the thing the ruler measures.

`src/game/flock.js` publishes what the tells need, as derived state beside the middle they are worked
out with: `pack.spread` (mean square distance from the middle, out of the `sx`/`sy`/`sq` sums - no
second walk of the crowd and one square root per pack, not per body) and `pack.pace` (the mean of
`speed * (1 - frost)` over the bodies actually in the pack, times `dive.mul`, so a half-chilled clump
promises a shorter lunge, which is what it does). Plus `beatProgress(pack)` with `braceProgress`
delegating to it, so the ring and the nose lights are provably one clock, and `isBracing`/`isCommitted`
taking a **pack** where `isBraced`/`isDiving` take a body - the eye draws per pack and should not have
to reach through a body to ask a question about its pack.

### The decision the measurement forced, and it is the finding of the session
`MIN_BODIES` is `ceil(pack.min / 2)` = 4, and that is **because a hive's brood is pairs**. Every mouth
lets out `each: 2` bodies and one pack per mouth (game/bosses.js `broodFrom`), so over a 20 s watch of
the second boss's cage the census counted 4-6 packs on the arena and *every one of them two bodies*,
and the number of clumps this file would draw is **zero**. The session 150 framing ("a wave of 40
bodies") is not forty bodies in a flock; it is thirty-two pairs on thirty-two clocks that happen to
be born in phase. A per-pack tell there would be thirty-two rings where the read wanted three, so the
tells are for the wave director's flocks and the hive keeps its nose lights. Worth knowing before
anyone redesigns that fight - and worth knowing that `balance.js`'s comment on the hive's spawn row
still claims "what comes out of one mouth bunches, commits and dives as one thing... what makes six
bodies one threat to read instead of six" while `each: 2` is on the row underneath it. That sentence
is stale prose about a two-body mouth and it is the next thing to settle.

### Numbers
- Reference run (`--seed 20261006 --trace`, aware bot, 10 min): **byte for byte session 150's run**,
  diffed against a `git worktree` of HEAD - `spread`/`pace` are read and never fed back, and the whole
  file is paint. Nothing to rebaseline.
- Cost, measured against HEAD with three clumps of fifteen braced on the glass (`.scratch/tell-cost.mjs`):
  **+3 strokes and +1 stamp per clump while bracing, +2 stamps per clump while diving**, no gradient,
  no blur, fills unchanged; frame cost 0.225 -> 0.237 ms at 45 flock bodies on this box. Three clumps
  is what a late run actually holds, so that is the ceiling, not a stress case.
- `tools/perf-probe.js --kind swarmling --bodies 200` is unchanged (1,765 ops mean, 0.093 vs 0.095 ms a
  step) because that scene plants loose bodies with no pack, which is itself worth knowing about the
  tool: it cannot price a flock at all today.
- Suite **2512**, up 16: 13 in the new `test/flock-tell.test.mjs` and 3 in `test/swarm.test.mjs`. The
  ones I would defend in review: *the line reaches exactly as far as the dive has left to fly* and then
  *the ground the light promised is the ground the pack walks* (paint at the commit, let the dive run,
  compare the middle's travel - the same bargain `test/beam-art.test.mjs` strikes for a beam); *the
  ring is sized by the clump it goes round*; *a pair draws nothing* at both ends of its dive; and *the
  frame asks for the ring*, which is the only test that the renderer hook exists.
- Released **v1.9.10**.

### Surprises and lessons
1. The census changed the design twice. First it killed "one tell per pack" as a fix for the hive (pairs),
   then it said the clump's spread barely tightens over the brace (p50 44.5 px gathering against 40.4
   braced - about a tenth of the ring's radius), so the *arc* carries the countdown and the radius only
   sizes the shape. I had written "the ring tightens with the bunching" in a comment before measuring it;
   the comment now says what is true. A guess about feel that a probe can check should be probed first.
2. **A mutation script has to prove it mutated.** My first one swapped text with `perl -0pi` and, on the
   swaps that silently did nothing (a `/` in the pattern against an `s///` delimiter), reported "did not
   apply", restored a backup... and still left two mutations sitting in `src/render/flock.js` from an
   earlier run, which is how one test went red for no reason an hour later. The replacement in
   `.scratch/mutate.sh` now counts hits with node, says `FOUND NOTHING` out loud, and all 12 mutations
   were seen and caught - including removing the call from `renderer.js`, which no direct-paint test can
   see. If a mutation harness is going to be trusted, the check is "did the file change", not "did the
   tests go red".
3. `test/swarm-art.test.mjs` caught this change honestly: its "a braced body lights its nose" test
   counted one light per body and got 21 for 20 bodies. Updated to `+1` for the clump and `+3` strokes,
   with a note on the dive test that a pack pinned at zero speed has no lunge to promise, so that test
   cannot see the line - it is a fact about the harness, and now it is written down instead of load-bearing.
4. The night (render/darkness.js) punches nothing for the swarm and did not before either: the veil
   lights the ship, shots, and a fight's own bodies. A flock that walked into the Eclipse's dark phase
   was already covered up; the tell goes the same way, and the file says so rather than leaving the next
   session to discover a hole that was never there.

### Left in the tree
`src/render/flock.js` (new), `src/game/flock.js` (two published numbers, one clock, two pack-level
predicates), `src/render/renderer.js` (one call), `test/flock-tell.test.mjs` (new, 13), `test/swarm.test.mjs`
(+3), `test/swarm-art.test.mjs` (two counts and a note), `PLAN.md` (the item, in *After 1.0*), CHANGELOG
and the release.

### Next
1. **Settle the hive's `each: 2`.** The row's own comment sells a six-body flock and the row ships a
   pair, and session 150 measured that fight as the *tightest* of the three at the game's own promise
   (58.3% free at its worst moment against the sun's 69.6 and the Warden's 87.6). Those two facts point
   the same way: fewer, bigger broods. Six bodies out of a lit mouth instead of two, on the same beat,
   is the same crowd and the same hull, but it is one clump to read instead of three pairs - and it is
   the same fight the new tells were built for, so the ruler and the ring would both be looking at it.
   `tools/boss-pressure.js` prices that (it reads the flock's own dive clock since session 150), and the
   claim to check is `worst`, not `standable`: a wave that has to be read as one thing should stop the
   room in fewer, more legible places. Start by re-running the census on the hive cage with a bigger
   `each` and checking the pack count and the tells-per-frame before touching the balance prose.
2. **`tools/perf-probe.js` has no flock scene.** It can say what 200 loose bodies cost and nothing about
   what three flocks cost, which is the shape the swarm actually arrives in. A `--flocks 3` scene would
   be a small addition to a tool that is otherwise honest about what it cannot measure.
3. Still open from earlier sessions: the **shot-speed line** (four seeds cannot tell 0.98 from 1.02;
   needs ~20), whether the **first two minutes** are too harsh for a new player (needs a human), and the
   `tierBonus.telegraph` sentence in PLAN that names a number which does not exist in this tree (session
   150's note; somebody has to decide whether a tier ladder of telegraphs is a thing to build or a
   sentence to delete).

## Session 152 - a mass's brood is one flock, so the hive's beat is a clump and wears the ring

### What was on the shelf
Session 151's first next-item: "settle the hive's `each: 2`". The clump's ring and dive line shipped the
session before and the census had said the second boss gives them nothing to draw - every mouth lets out
`each: 2` bodies as a pack of its own, so 6-12 packs of two bodies in the cage and zero clumps - while
the comment on that very balance row was still claiming that what comes out of a mouth bunches, commits
and dives as one thing and that this is what makes six bodies one threat to read. So either the sentence
was a leftover from a row that never shipped, or the sentence was the design and the number was the
accident. It measured as the second: the brood are the kind's whole idea and the fight was spending them
in twos.

### The answer I tried first, and why it is wrong
`.scratch/hive-brood.mjs` is a new census that patches `phases[].spawn` at runtime (a share and an `each`
per phase, which phase to drive the hull down to, how long to watch), so the sweep cost no edits to
balance.js. The obvious move is fewer, bigger mouths for the same crowd: `share: 0.17, each: 4` for
phase 1 and `share: 0.17, each: 6` for phase 2 - one mouth a beat instead of two and three, the same four
and six bodies, and the census liked it: clumps of 4 and 6, one tell a frame at p90. The *lever* did not.
`lightTheCore` lights `max(1, round(standing * share))` mouths, and that share is the whole of the reason
to shoot the honeycomb; at 0.17 a six-cell mass and a two-cell mass light the same one mouth and breaking
the mass stops thinning the brood, which is exactly what `test/hive.test.mjs`'s "the smaller the mass,
the smaller the swarm" is there to catch. It went red and it was right. **`share` is a lever and not a
size**: number of mouths, which is the reward for breaking them; `each` is what one mouth is worth; a
beat is their product and neither can be bought without paying in bodies.

### What landed
**A mass's brood is one flock.** `game/bosses.js` `openTheCore` makes the flock once, at the first mouth
that actually opens (`broodPack`, which also puts it in `world.flocks`), and every cell that beat lit puts
its `each` bodies into that one. It works because the mouths a beat lights are *consecutive* round the
ring (`lightTheCore` walks `cells[(core.turn + i) % standing]`): neighbours 50 px apart on a full hive,
so the bevy leaves as one bunch and the flock's own `keep` of 92 px closes it the rest of the way. No
number in balance.js moved. Phase 1 is one clump of four where it was two pairs, phase 2 one of six where
it was three, and phase 3 is untouched because a fragment has one mouth to light - and that stays: a
piece has three cells, a share of three rounds to one mouth, two bodies is as big a flock as a piece can
field, and three pieces are three places to read already. The last phase keeps its nose lights and the
split's row now says so.

`isClump` and `MIN_BODIES` moved out of `render/flock.js` into `game/flock.js`, next to the pack they are a
fact about, so the painter and the fight answer "is this a clump" off one number - and four bodies is no
longer a coincidence but exactly where a hive's beat sits. The three places that said "one pack per cell"
in prose (the hive row, the split row, `openTheCore`) now say what happens.

### Numbers
- Census, shipped rows, parked ship, 40 s, per phase. **Before:** packs p50 6 / 9 / 12, every pack two
  bodies, clumps big enough to be drawn: zero. **After:** 3 / 3 / 12 packs of 4 / 6 / 2 bodies, and what
  a frame is asked to draw is at most **one ring and one line in phase 1**, **two rings and one line in
  phase 2** (p90 one ring), and still nothing in the third. Spread while bracing 27-31 px, which is the
  same clump the wave flocks arrive at, so none of last session's sizes needed touching.
- `tools/boss-pressure.js --boss hive`, three seeds, against a `git worktree` of HEAD. **Near watch
  (8 s, what a run is actually left with):** `crowd` (12/23/41) and `sent/s` (1.00/0.75/0.75) identical in
  every row, standable within half a point, and the worst moment level or looser - phase 1 73.2/72.8/72.0
  free becomes 72.1/72.3/71.6, phase 2 62.9/71.2/71.2 becomes 65.8/70.8/71.3, phase 3 58.3/49.5/51.8
  becomes 57.9/62.5/55.9. **Long watch (40 s):** phases 1 and 2 *loosen* (phase 1's worst 63.8/64.8/63.6
  becomes 71.1/67.5/66.4 - three dive bearings became one) and phase 3 reads 6-12 points *tighter*. That
  last one is the tool's own printed caveat and not the fight: nothing shoots back, so after a minute a
  passive ship is being camped by 118 bodies and a clump camps closer than a pair drifts, over an
  arrive-disc of some 430 px. The tool says read the near one; the near one says the fight is the same
  fight with three things to read where there were six.
- Reference run (`--seed 20261006 --trace`, aware bot, 10 min): **byte for byte the run it was**, diffed
  line for line against the worktree - a wave's swarm is built by `waves.js` and never passes through
  `broodFrom`, and the fight that run meets is the Warden. `tools/difficulty-arc.js --runs 24 --seed 300`
  is identical too: 21 of 24 careless runs die before 4:00, so no careless run ever meets the hive.
- Suite **2514**, one up. `test/hive.test.mjs`: "what comes out of one mouth is one pack" became **"one
  beat lets out one flock, however many mouths opened"** - it asserts first that the row lights more than
  one mouth, so it cannot go blind by accident, then one flock, `pack.n` the whole brood, and `isClump`;
  and **"a piece lets out its own flock, and the three of them are the fight"** - three flocks to a beat,
  each flock's bodies all nearest the same piece, and no piece's brood big enough to be drawn as a clump.
  `test/flock-tell.test.mjs`'s threshold test reads the *split* row for its pair now, and also paints the
  pair to prove it gets no ring. Mutation check: putting the merge back (every mouth its own flock) goes
  red on the new test and on nothing else.

### Surprises and lessons
1. **`share` is a lever, not a size** - see above. If a later session wants bigger broods it has to say
   which it is buying: more bodies, or the same bodies closer. Only the first belongs in `each`.
2. **`simulate.js --at 600` does not put you in the second boss's fight.** The schedule still walks the
   Warden first, so all twelve of those runs died to the wave crowd and measured nothing about the hive.
   Boss fights are measured with `tools/boss-pressure.js` and the census; the bot's arc does not even
   reach 10:00 (21 of 24 careless runs are dead before 4:00, which is the open "first two minutes"
   question wearing a different hat).
3. The same ruler, watched for 8 s and for 40 s, disagreed about the third phase by twenty points. Both
   are written above rather than the flattering one, and the reason is in the tool's own caveats. A ruler
   whose sample is a passive ship is a ruler of a state no run is in, and the longer you watch it the more
   true that becomes.
4. The census script is the cheapest thing in the box that can answer "what would the eye be asked for",
   and patching `BALANCE` in one script is much faster than editing a row, running, and putting it back.

### Left in the tree
`src/game/bosses.js` (`openTheCore` makes one flock, new `broodPack`, `broodFrom` takes one),
`src/game/flock.js` (`MIN_BODIES` and `isClump`, and a `balance.js` import - no cycle, balance imports
only palette), `src/render/flock.js` (imports the answer and says who is not a clump now),
`src/game/balance.js` (three stale sentences about one pack per mouth, comments only),
`test/hive.test.mjs` (two tests rewritten or added, `broods` and `nearest` helpers),
`test/flock-tell.test.mjs` (the threshold test and the pair's own paint), `.scratch/hive-brood.mjs`,
PLAN, CHANGELOG and the release.

### Next
1. **`tools/perf-probe.js` still has no flock scene** - straight from session 151's list and more true
   now: three clumps bracing is what the frame is actually asked to draw, in waves and in the hive both,
   and the probe can only price 200 loose bodies with no pack at all. A `--flocks 3` scene is a small
   addition to a tool that is otherwise honest about what it cannot measure.
2. **Is the ring too loud, and is the hive's beat too quiet?** The eye has an answer for both now and no
   human has looked. The census can count shapes per frame; only a person can say whether one ring per
   clump over thirty pairs' worth of nose lights is the right amount of light on a late hive. Worth

3. Still open from earlier sessions: the **shot-speed line** (four seeds cannot tell 0.98 from 1.02;
   needs ~20), whether the **first two minutes** are too harsh for a new player (needs a human), and the

## Session 153 - the ruler could not price a brood; now it can, in operations - and the byte ruler's kind table had been printing nine identical rows

### What was on the shelf
Session 152's next-item 1, verbatim: "`tools/perf-probe.js` still has no flock scene". It was more true
after 152 than before it. A planted swarmling with no pack chases the ship (game/kinds.js
`walksFlocking` falls back to that when `packOf(enemy)` is null), so every crowd scene in the ruler was
pricing the swarm as if it were another drifter: no middle to steer by, no beat to keep, no ring and no
line to draw. And three clumps bracing is precisely what a late frame is asked to draw - in the waves and
in the hive's beat both.

### The two scenes, and why they are a pair
`brood` plants three clumps of fourteen swarmlings as real packs (game/flock.js `newPack`, in
`world.flocks`, every body pointing at its pack) and `loose` plants the same bodies in the same clumps
and then takes the packs back out again (`unpacked`). So "what does a flock cost" is a subtraction
between two printed rows and not a sentence in a comment. Both numbers are the game's: three clumps is
what session 151's census counted on the glass at a time, and fourteen is the middle of the pack the
wave director may buy (`kinds.swarmling.pack.min` to `.into`). The clumps are planted part way through
their own gathering beat and staggered from each other, because packs are born seconds apart and keep
the clock they were born with - plant them in step and the scene is a volley the game never fields.

Three more things came with them, because the scene is not honest without them:

- **A scene may name the window it has to be watched for.** A pack's whole beat is 4.6 s and a brace is
  0.7 s of it, so the ruler's default two-second window can paint an entire brood with no tell on it and
  report the clump as cheap as a loose crowd. Both flock rows ask for `ceil(FLOCK_CYCLE)` = 5 s, the
  header says which windows were measured when they disagree, and `--seconds` still outranks a scene
  because the flag is the question.
- **`--flocks N`, and `--scene a,b`.** `--flocks 0` asks the brood's question of any scene; a comma list
  is what makes a row and its control readable in one run rather than two.
- **`measureBeats`, and a fourth budget.** A scene's mean over a window cannot see a tell at all, so each
  clump's clock is pinned half-way through `gathering`, `braced` and `diving` and one frame is painted
  per beat; the gathering frame is the baseline (a gathering pack draws nothing) and the two deltas are
  the art's shape counted: **the brace is +18.0 operations a clump (3 strokes, 15 stamps) and the dive
  +16.0 (0 strokes, 16 stamps)**, against `TELL_OPS = 40`. The test asserts the shapes themselves -
  three strokes and one light for the ring plus a nose light per body, a stamp per body on the line, no
  gradient and no shadow on either - so a fourth shape or a blur on every clump has to be argued about.
  Three clumps is what a late run holds, so a dear tell is paid three times on one frame.

### What it measured
| scene | bodies | packs | step ms | ops mean | ops worst |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| the crowd at the body wall | 200 | 0 | 0.111 | 2,951 | 3,012 |
| the brood, in clumps | 42 | 3.0 | 0.016 | 1,301 | 1,347 |
| the same brood, loose | 42 | 0 | 0.017 | 1,285 | 1,347 |

A whole flock of them costs **+16 operations a frame** over the same bodies loose, and **nothing
measurable in the step** - which is the right shape for an answer, because a pack is arithmetic on the
crowd it describes and not a second crowd walking beside it. The two halves of the ruler reconcile:
a clump braces 0.7 s of its 4.6 s cycle and dives for 0.5 s of it, three staggered clumps is about 0.45
of a clump braced and 0.33 diving on any one frame, and 0.45 × 18 + 0.33 × 16 ≈ 14 against the 16
measured. What the brood's frame is made of is the 900 sparks and the 42 bodies, not the tells: 1,251
of its 1,301 operations are there with every clump gathering, and the crowd at the ceiling - 200 loose
bodies, no packs, nothing braced - is still 2,951, which is the wall this frame has to live inside.

### The bug this found in the other ruler
`tools/alloc-probe.js --kinds` builds one row per kind and has stamped the kind onto the row's name
since it was written - and spread the measuring child's own row *after* the stamp, so the stamp was
overwritten and all nine rows printed as "the schedule at full crowd". Nobody could read that table, so
nobody ran it, so it had no test, so it stayed. Fixed, and now:

- the stamp is applied after the reading (`rowName`, and a test that reads what the tool printed, which
  is the only place the bug was ever visible);
- **a crowd of one kind is a price list and not a wall**: `--kind` and `--kinds` rows are measured and
  never gated, and every one of them over `BODY_BYTES` is named under the table, so ungated is not the
  same as silent;
- a `noBytes` scene is out of a default byte run and out of the byte gate even when asked for by name.
  The brood's 39 B a body is mostly what 900 sparks cost, not what a clump does; a clump is priced in
  operations, which is the currency it actually moves.

And the now-readable table says: drifter, weaver, spitter, tank, bomber and sniper throw away nothing a
step; the **darter 7 B a body** (it files sounds), the **swarmling 32 B** and the **shielder 48 B**.
PLAN section 2's "no allocation inside the per-frame loops" is not true of two of the nine kinds, and
has not been for as long as the table has been unread. Not chased here - it is its own session.

### Surprises and lessons
1. **A hold that repairs a scene can become an engine.** `holdScene` puts missing clumps back, and
   `updateFlocks` throws away a pack whose last body is gone - so a planting that ever attaches bodies
   to no pack makes the hold add a fresh clump every step, forever. The mutation "a body is planted
   without its pack" used to hang the test file for a quarter of an hour; the guard is that a clump is
   part of the crowd, so the room for one is measured in the crowd, and the same mutation now fails
   eleven tests in about a second. There is a test for both halves: a clump that is *really* gone comes
   back, and one with no room is not conjured.
2. **Timing assertions that pass alone and fail inside `node --test`.** The brood-vs-control step read
   0.163 ms against 0.022 ms with the rest of the suite running alongside, and 0.016 against 0.017 on a
   quiet box. Operations are counted and exact, so they can be strict; a tenth-of-a-millisecond step on
   a 42-body scene cannot be. The step claim is now floored at `max(3 × control, 0.25 ms)` and says so
   in the message, and the ratchet on a step stays where it always was, in `SIM_STEP_MS`.
3. **A test helper can measure the mistake the scene exists to avoid.** The helper forced a one-second
   window on every scene, which for the flock pair is exactly the coin-toss-on-whether-a-tell-is-on-the-
   glass. The helpers now honour a scene's own window, which is why the flock tests are the slow ones.
4. Cross-checking two rulers is how a wrong claim dies. The brood looked like a byte wall at 39 B a body
   until its loose control showed 32 B of that belongs to the *kind* - and then the operations ruler
   showed the flock itself is 16 ops a frame. Same bodies, two currencies, one answer each.
5. `.scratch/alloc-sites.js` (the inspector's sampling heap profiler) reads 3.7 B a step on a load the
   probe reads at 3.2 KB. Both are true: a sampling *heap* profile counts what stayed alive and the
   probe counts what was thrown away. So the crowd leaks nothing and generates a scavenge's worth of
   garbage every couple of seconds, which is a different problem and a real one.

### Left in the tree
`tools/perf-probe.js` (the brood and its control, `--flocks`, scene windows, `measureBeats`, `TELL_OPS`,
the guarded hold, and a header that now says what each of its four budgets is allowed to mean),
`tools/alloc-probe.js` (`rowName`, price lists, `overBudgetRows`, `noBytes`), `src/game/flock.js`
(`BEATS` exported so a tool can name a beat instead of spelling 'brace' and hoping - no behaviour
change: the reference trace is byte for byte the run it was), `test/perf-probe.test.mjs` (14 → 22),
`test/alloc-probe.test.mjs` (14 → 17), suite 2515 → 2526. In `.scratch`: `mutate-beats.mjs` (ten
mutations, all ten caught), `brood-ops.mjs`, `tell-cost.mjs`, `alloc-sites.js`, `bytes-per-step.js`.
**No release**: nothing a player sees or feels changed, which is the same call session 150 made for a
ruler-only session.

### Next
1. **The shielder and the swarmling allocate, and the other seven kinds do not**: 48 B and 32 B a body a
   step on a crowd of one kind, where `BODY_BYTES` is 5 and a crowd of drifters is 0. Start by settling
   whether a *mixed* crowd pays its share: the probe reads the gated schedule crowd at 0 B a body, which
   cannot be right if a dozen shielders at 48 B are standing in it, and my crude independent script
   (`.scratch/bytes-per-step.js`, no GC-watching, and it caught itself lying once) says 3.5 B a body for
   the same load. So: re-check the mixed reading first, then name the line, then take it out. A scavenge
   of this heap is 0.85-1.12 ms, and a roomful of shielders is what would make one every two seconds
   instead of every twelve.
2. Whether the per-kind rows should become a gate once those two kinds are honest - and whether
   `BODY_BYTES` should then be asked of a crowd of the *worst* kind the director can field rather than of
   the mixed one.
3. Is the ring too loud, and is the hive's beat too quiet? Unchanged from session 152: the census can
   count shapes per frame, only a person can say whether one ring per clump over thirty pairs' worth of
   nose lights is the right amount of light on a late hive.
4. Still open from earlier sessions: the **shot-speed line** (four seeds cannot tell 0.98 from 1.02;
   needs ~20), whether the **first two minutes** are too harsh for a new player (needs a human), the
   `tierBonus.telegraph` sentence in PLAN that names a number which does not exist in this tree, and
   PLAN's browser half of the performance pass - which now also has a brood row (1,301 operations a
   frame at 42 bodies) for whoever puts the F3 plate up to compare a real late flight against.
